chapters.title: 序章 · 雪山采冰人
chapters.en:
Long ago, atop a mountain high above the kingdom of Arendelle, a group of strong men were hard at work. They were ice harvesters, men who cut and hauled huge blocks of ice from the mountain lakes. Horses stood at attention, waiting with empty wagons to be filled. The ice blocks were hoisted into the wagons; soon they would be taken down to the village to sell. It was a dangerous business. One slip could send a block hurtling down the mountainside—or even worse, falling on a man and crushing him.

A boy stood in the shadows watching the workmen. He kept a small sled at his side. His name was Kristoff, and he desperately wanted to join the ice harvesters, but he was too young. Standing next to him was his friend Sven, a baby reindeer. Kristoff imagined the two of them taking a sled full of ice blocks into the village of Arendelle. Sven sniffed the cold air and glanced at the big blocks of ice. They looked very heavy. He snorted but didn’t move a hoof.

As evening approached, Kristoff finally convinced Sven to carry a small load of ice on their sled. By now, the men had lit several lanterns and were finishing loading their own wagons. Kristoff crept forward and was able to grab a small block of ice. He finally wrestled the block onto his sled and attached Sven’s harness.

Wagon by wagon, the ice harvesters headed down the mountain roads. Kristoff trailed behind with Sven, steering his own small wagon down the bumpy path.

Above them all, the northern lights spread across the dark sky, creating waves of gossamer green light. The magical glow pulsed as it rolled over the mountains, down toward the kingdom below.
chapters.zh:
很久以前，在阿伦黛尔王国上方的高山上，一群强壮的男人正在辛勤劳作。他们是采冰人——从山间湖泊中切割、拖运巨大冰块的人。马匹肃立待命，空着的雪橇等待着被装满。冰块被吊上雪橇，很快就会被运下山，送到村子里售卖。这是一门危险的行当：稍一失足，一块冰便会顺着山坡呼啸滚落——更糟的是，砸在某人身上将他压碎。

一个男孩站在阴影里望着这些工人，身边放着一架小雪橇。他叫克斯托夫，一心想加入采冰人的行列，却还太小。站在他身旁的是他的朋友斯文，一头小驯鹿。克斯托夫想象着他们俩驾着满载冰块的雪橇，驶进阿伦黛尔的村庄。斯文嗅了嗅寒冷的空气，瞥了一眼那些巨大的冰块——看起来沉得很。他喷了喷鼻息，却一步也没动。

夜色渐临，克斯托夫终于说服斯文在他们的雪橇上载一小块冰。此时，大人们已经点亮数盏灯笼，正装载完自己的雪橇。克斯托夫悄悄挪上前，抓到了一小块冰。他费了好大劲才把冰块弄上自己的雪橇，系好了斯文的挽具。

采冰人一辆接一辆地驶下山道。克斯托夫赶着斯文，驾着他的小雪橇，沿着坑洼不平的小路跟在后面。

在他们头顶，北极光铺展在夜空中，漾起一层层薄纱般的绿光。那魔幻的光晕随着山峦起伏、脉动，一路倾泻向山下的王国。

chapters.title: 第一章 · 极光下的女孩
chapters.en:
In a grassy valley next to a deep fjord, the castle of Arendelle lay silent in the night. The bright luster of the northern lights danced across the windows, waking a small girl. She sat up and grinned to see the wonderful green light.

The girl jumped out of bed and tiptoed across the room to wake her older sister. “Elsa, Elsa!” she said urgently. “Wake up!”

Elsa, who was eight years old, grumbled and ducked under the covers. “Anna, go back to sleep.”

But Anna wouldn’t give up. “I just can’t. The sky’s awake, so I’m awake, and so we have to play,” she said. “Do you want to build a snowman?”

Elsa’s eyes popped open. That got her attention.

The girls were the daughters of Arendelle’s king and queen, and the best of friends. Elsa couldn’t resist Anna’s begging. The sisters ran down the hallway in their nightgowns, laughing as they hurried along. Entering the Great Hall, where all the royal balls were held, they turned to each other.

“Are you ready?” Elsa asked, smiling.

“Yes, yes!” Anna cried, reaching out to tickle her sister.

Elsa giggled, and suddenly, snowflakes seemed to burst in a flurry from her hands!

Anna clapped happily. She knew that her sister had a very special talent: she could create snow and ice, even in the middle of summer!

With a twirl and a wave of her hands, Elsa magically summoned her icy powers. Quickly, she filled the Great Hall with mounds of fluffy snow, turning it into a winter playground. Then she stomped her feet and ice swept across the floor. She laughed to see little Anna hopping around joyfully.

Together, they went to work building their snowman. Anna did her best to roll out the snowman’s body. Then she ran to get a carrot for the nose. “Snowman!” she exclaimed proudly.

Elsa laughed at the lopsided snowman. “Hi, I’m Olaf,” she said in a deep voice, pretending to be the snowman. “And I like warm hugs.”

The girls danced around their funny snowman.

Then Elsa gathered her icy magic and made a swooping ice slide. Anna squealed with delight. She climbed to the top of the slide, then zoomed down and soared up again along the icy curve. Elsa quickly created another slide to catch Anna as she came down. The little girl gained speed and was tossed upward again. Elsa had to work fast to keep pace with Anna. She kept making more slides so her sister could stay aloft as she flew around the room.

“Anna, slow down,” Elsa said, starting to get worried. “It’s too high!”

But Anna was having fun. The little princess was fearless, jumping and sliding to each new slide as quickly as Elsa made it. Elsa raised her hand to create the next slide, but suddenly, her foot slipped. As she stumbled, her magic went awry. Her frozen blast caught the side of Anna’s head, right through her curls.

Anna gasped and fell to the ground, unconscious.

“Anna!” Elsa shouted, running to her sister. She lifted Anna up and felt her cold, shivering body. A lock of Anna’s hair had turned pure white where the magic had hit it. “Mama! Papa!” Elsa cried desperately.

As she called for help and her worry increased, icicles formed on the ceiling, and frozen spikes grew tall around the girls.

The king and queen burst into the Great Hall to find their daughters huddled in a frozen landscape. They knew that Elsa had a special ability to create ice, but this was more than they’d ever seen. “Elsa,” the king cried. “This is getting out of hand!”

“I’m sorry,” Elsa replied in distress. “I didn’t mean it!”

“Anna!” the queen gasped, and ran toward her little girl.
chapters.zh:
在一道深邃峡湾旁的青翠山谷里，阿伦黛尔的城堡在夜色中静默无声。北极光的璀璨流光在窗上舞动，唤醒了一个小女孩。她坐起身，看到那美妙的绿光，咧嘴笑了起来。

女孩跳下床，踮着脚尖穿过房间去叫醒姐姐。「艾莎，艾莎！」她急切地说，「醒醒！」

八岁的艾莎嘟囔着缩进被子里。「安娜，回去睡觉。」

可安娜不肯放弃。「我就是睡不着。天空醒着，所以我醒着，那我们就得玩呀，」她说，「你想堆个雪人吗？」

艾莎一下子睁大了眼睛。这话成功引起了她的注意。

两姐妹是阿伦黛尔国王与王后的女儿，也是最好的朋友。艾莎抵挡不住安娜的央求。姐妹俩穿着睡衣跑过走廊，一路笑着匆匆前行。走进举办过所有王室舞会的大厅，她们相视而立。

「准备好了吗？」艾莎微笑着问。

「准备好了，准备好了！」安娜喊着，伸手去挠姐姐的痒。

艾莎咯咯笑起来，忽然，雪花仿佛从她手中纷纷扬扬地迸发出来！

安娜开心地拍手。她知道姐姐有一种很特别的天赋：她能制造冰雪，哪怕在盛夏之中！

艾莎旋身挥手，施展起她神奇的冰雪之力。转眼间，她让大堆蓬松的雪填满大厅，把它变成了冬日游乐场。接着她跺了跺脚，冰层便漫过地面。看着小安娜欢快地蹦跳，她笑了起来。

姐妹俩一起动手堆起了雪人。安娜尽力滚出雪人的身体，然后跑去拿了一根胡萝卜当鼻子。「雪人！」她骄傲地宣布。

艾莎看着这个歪歪扭扭的雪人笑了。「嗨，我是雪宝，」她压低嗓音，假装自己是那个雪人，「我喜欢温暖的拥抱。」

两个女孩围着滑稽的雪人跳起舞来。

随后，艾莎凝聚冰雪魔法，造出一道蜿蜒的冰滑梯。安娜高兴得尖叫起来。她爬到滑梯顶端，嗖地滑下，又顺着冰弧冲天飞起。艾莎连忙再变出一道滑梯，在安娜下落时接住她。小女孩越滑越快，又被抛向高处。艾莎得动作飞快才能跟上安娜的节奏——她不断造出新的滑梯，好让妹妹在房间里飞翔时始终有依托。

「安娜，慢一点，」艾莎开始担心起来，「太高了！」

可安娜正玩在兴头上。小公主毫无惧色，艾莎每造出一道新滑梯，她就立刻跳上去、滑下去。艾莎举起手准备再变下一道，脚却忽然一滑。她踉跄之间，魔法失了准头——那道冰劲击中了安娜的头部，正穿过她的卷发。

安娜倒抽一口气，瘫倒在地，失去了意识。

「安娜！」艾莎喊着跑向妹妹，把她抱起来，摸到她冰冷发抖的身体。魔法击中的地方，安娜的一缕头发变成了纯白。「妈妈！爸爸！」艾莎绝望地呼喊。

她越是焦急呼救，天花板上的冰柱就越发成形，四周的冰刺也越长越高，将姐妹俩团团围住。

国王与王后冲进大厅，只见女儿们蜷缩在一片冰封的景象中。他们知道艾莎有造冰的特别能力，可眼前这一幕远超他们的想象。「艾莎，」国王喊道，「这已经失控了！」

「对不起，」艾莎惶恐地回答，「我不是故意的！」

「安娜！」王后惊呼，朝小女儿跑去。

sentences.en: A lock of Anna’s hair had turned pure white where the magic had hit it.
sentences.zh: 魔法击中的地方，安娜的一缕头发变成了纯白。

sentences.en: “Mama! Papa!” Elsa cried desperately.
sentences.zh: 「妈妈！爸爸！」艾莎绝望地呼喊。

sentences.en: As she called for help and her worry increased, icicles formed on the ceiling, and frozen spikes grew tall around the girls.
sentences.zh: 她越是焦急呼救，天花板上的冰柱就越发成形，四周的冰刺也越长越高，将姐妹俩团团围住。

sentences.en: The king and queen burst into the Great Hall to find their daughters huddled in a frozen landscape.
sentences.zh: 国王与王后冲进大厅，只见女儿们蜷缩在一片冰封的景象中。

sentences.en: They knew that Elsa had a special ability to create ice, but this was more than they’d ever seen.
sentences.zh: 他们知道艾莎有造冰的特别能力，可眼前这一幕远超他们的想象。

sentences.en: “Elsa,” the king cried. “This is getting out of hand!”
sentences.zh: 「艾莎，」国王喊道，「这已经失控了！」

sentences.en: “I’m sorry,” Elsa replied in distress. “I didn’t mean it!”
sentences.zh: 「对不起，」艾莎惶恐地回答，「我不是故意的！」

sentences.en: “Anna!” the queen gasped, and ran toward her little girl.
sentences.zh: 「安娜！」王后惊呼，朝小女儿跑去。

chapters.title: 第二章 · 尘封的古书
chapters.en:
The castle’s library was dark, but the king knew what he was looking for: an ancient book filled with knowledge from centuries past. When he found it, he pulled it from the shelf and quickly flipped through the pages to the section he needed. In it was a drawing of a troll, which seemed to be holding the northern lights in its hands. In front of the troll, a wounded human lay quiet while the troll used the magic of the northern lights to heal him. The king turned the page and spotted a crumbling document tucked into the book. He carefully unfolded the yellowed map.

Wasting no time, the king and queen threw on their cloaks, bundled up their daughters, and ordered that the horses be saddled. The royal family hurried away from the castle. The queen traveled on her own horse with Elsa, while the king held Anna in his arms. The horses thundered up the mountain path.

Kristoff and Sven were walking down the rocky mountain path under the bright glow of the northern lights. But as the rumble of hooves filled the air, they moved aside, wary of the approaching horses. They watched the riders gallop past, leaving a trail of ice behind them.

Curious, Kristoff and Sven followed the travelers to a ridge above a mountain valley. The two hid behind a rock and watched as the horses whinnied and came to a stop.

The king and queen dismounted. The king held a young girl to his shoulder; the queen held the hand of a slightly older girl.

“Please, help!” the king cried out. “My daughter!”

The hillside appeared empty at first. Then a pile of rocks rolled down the hillside. Suddenly, the rocks unfolded themselves into legs and arms and stood up, revealing themselves to be small gray creatures—they weren’t rocks at all! “Trolls,” Kristoff whispered to Sven.

At that moment, a rock next to Kristoff jumped up, turning into a short troll woman covered with moss. Her name was Hulda.

“Shush,” Hulda told Kristoff absently. “I’m trying to listen.” Then, startled, Hulda looked more closely at Kristoff, realizing for the first time that he was not a troll. Her face broke into a grin, and she reached out to give Kristoff and Sven big hugs. “Cuties!” she said, laughing.

In the valley, the king stood with his daughters as Pabbie, a very old troll, made his way through the crowd to gaze at the princesses.

First he looked at Elsa. “Was she born with the powers or cursed?” he asked.

“Born,” the king answered. “And they’re getting stronger.”

The troll then turned his attention to Anna, who was still unconscious. “You are lucky it wasn’t her heart that was struck,” he noted. “The heart is not so easily changed, but the head can be persuaded.” He paused. “We should remove all the magic, even memories of magic, to be safe.”

The king nodded. “Do what you must,” he said.

With a gentle touch of his fingers, the troll pulled a series of glowing memories from little Anna’s head. The memories hovered in the air as the troll transformed them into more sensible scenes. Instead of a magical snowman in the ballroom, Anna would now remember a winter scene in the courtyard. Instead of snowflakes in the hallway, she would remember snowflakes falling outside the window. All the magical moments she had shared with Elsa were gone, replaced with normal moments. The only remnant of her magical accident was the streak of white in her hair.

“There,” said Pabbie when he was finished. “She will remember the fun, but not the magic.”

“She won’t remember that I have powers?” Elsa asked.

“No,” Pabbie said.

“It’s for the best,” the king told her.

“Listen to me, Elsa,” Pabbie said. “Your power will only grow. There is beauty in it, but also great danger.”

As he spoke, the troll conjured up an image of an older Elsa in the sky. The image twirled gracefully, surrounded by beautiful snowflakes.

Then, amid the northern lights, the snowflakes turned into sharp spikes. The spectre of a crowd joined Elsa in the sky—the people used the icy spikes as weapons, attacking Elsa’s glowing effigy.

“You must learn to control your power,” Pabbie continued. “Fear will be your enemy.”

The king hugged Elsa close. “We’ll protect her,” he promised. “We’ll lock the gates. We’ll reduce the staff and keep her powers hidden from everyone…including Anna.”
chapters.zh:
城堡的图书馆里一片昏暗，但国王清楚自己要找什么：一本汇聚了数百年前知识的古书。他找到后，从书架上抽出，飞快地翻到需要的那一页。书里画着一只山精，仿佛双手捧着北极光；山精面前，一个受伤的人静静躺着，山精正用北极光的魔法为他疗伤。国王翻过一页，发现书里夹着一份泛黄的脆薄文件。他小心地展开那张发黄的地图。

国王与王后一刻不耽搁，披上斗篷，把女儿们裹得严严实实，下令备马。王室一家匆匆离开城堡。王后带着艾莎骑自己的马，国王则把安娜抱在怀里。马蹄声如雷，沿山路而上。

克斯托夫和斯文正走在崎岖的山路上，头顶是明亮的北极光。可当马蹄的轰鸣充斥空气，他们退到一旁，警惕着逼近的马群。他们看着骑手疾驰而过，身后留下一道冰痕。

出于好奇，克斯托夫和斯文跟着旅人来到一处山谷上方的山脊。两人躲在岩石后，望着马匹嘶鸣着停下脚步。

国王与王后下了马。国王把一个小女孩扛在肩头，王后则牵着稍大些的女孩的手。

「求求你，救救她！」国王高声呼救，「我的女儿！」

山坡起初看似空无一人。接着，一堆石头顺着坡滚落。忽然，那些石头舒展开手脚，站了起来——它们根本不是石头，而是灰色的小生物！「山精，」克斯托夫对斯文低声说。

就在这时，克斯托夫身旁的一块石头跳了起来，变成一只满身苔藓的矮个子女山精。她叫布尔达（Hulda）。

「嘘，」布尔达心不在焉地对克斯托夫说，「我正试着听呢。」随即她一愣，凑近打量克斯托夫，这才头一回意识到他不是山精。她咧嘴一笑，伸手给了克斯托夫和斯文一个大大的拥抱。「小可爱！」她笑着说。

山谷里，国王带着两个女儿站着，年迈的山精大帕比（Pabbie）穿过人群，端详起两位公主。

他先看艾莎。「她是与生俱来就有这力量，还是被诅咒的？」他问。

「与生俱来，」国王答道，「而且越来越强了。」

山精随即把注意力转向仍昏迷不醒的安娜。「幸好被击中的不是她的心脏，」他提醒道，「心没那么容易改变，但脑子可以被说服。」他顿了顿，「为保万全，我们应当移除所有魔法，连同对魔法的记忆一起。」

国王点点头。「该怎么做就怎么做，」他说。

山精用手指轻轻一触，从小小的安娜脑中取出一连串发光的记忆。那些记忆悬浮在空中，山精将它们改写成更寻常的画面：不再是舞厅里神奇的雪人，安娜今后会记得庭院里的一场冬景；不再是走廊上的雪花，她会记得窗外飘落的雪。她与艾莎共享的所有魔法瞬间都被抹去，换成了平常的时刻。那场魔法意外的唯一痕迹，就是她头发上那一缕白发。

「好了，」大帕比做完后说，「她会记得那些欢乐，却不记得魔法。」

「她不会记得我有魔法了？」艾莎问。

「不会，」大帕比说。

「这样最好，」国王对她说。

「听我说，艾莎，」大帕比道，「你的力量只会增长。它其中有美，也有巨大的危险。」

说话间，山精在空中幻化出长大后的艾莎的形象。那影像优雅地旋转，被美丽的雪花环绕。

接着，在北极光中，雪花化作尖锐的冰刺。一群幽灵般的民众加入空中的艾莎——人们把冰刺当武器，攻击着艾莎发光的虚像。

「你必须学会控制自己的力量，」大帕比继续道，「恐惧将是你的敌人。」

国王把艾莎紧紧搂在怀里。「我们会保护她，」他承诺，「我们会锁上城门，裁减侍从，把她的力量对所有人隐瞒……包括安娜。」

chapters.title: 第三章 · 紧闭的宫门
chapters.en:
Back at the castle, the king and queen immediately ordered that the castle gates be locked. All the doors were closed and the windows shuttered. They kept the girls secluded and no longer opened the castle to visitors. The family stayed hidden, tucked away inside their walled kingdom.

The king and queen acted just as cautiously inside the castle. As the princesses grew, their parents did everything they could to ensure that Elsa learned to control herself. That meant the girls were hardly ever together. Nor did Elsa seek Anna out, since she was afraid she might accidentally hurt her. Day after day, Elsa spent most of her time training to be the next ruler—and learning to keep her powers in check.

The training was difficult, and Elsa often felt unable to contain her magic. Ice seemed to form on her fingertips whenever she laughed or cried or became upset.

Worried, the king gave Elsa a pair of leather gloves. He advised her to keep them on at all times, and reminded her that she had to hide her icy magic in order to stay safe. “Conceal it,” he told her.

“Don’t feel it,” she answered.

“Don’t let it show,” he agreed.

The years slipped by. Anna spent most of her time alone. Sometimes she played with her dolls; sometimes she pretended to have conversations with painted portraits in the gallery. But she was lonely.

Time after time, she knocked on Elsa’s door, pleading with her sister to come out and play. But Elsa never did. The memory of their friendship was slowly fading.

One day, Anna peered out her window and saw snow falling in the royal gardens. She raced down the hallway to her sister’s room. “Do you want to build a snowman?” she called through the closed door.

There was no reply from inside. The door did not open. Eventually, Anna went out into the courtyard and tried to build a snowman by herself. After rolling out a lopsided ball, she glanced up at Elsa’s window and thought she saw someone smiling down at her. But when she looked again, the face was gone.

Without any memory of Elsa’s magic, Anna had no idea why she was always alone. Over time, she simply came to accept that her sister’s coldness was part of who she was. She didn’t know that Elsa was lonely too, and that she missed Anna as much as Anna missed her. Elsa longed to play with Anna but was fearful of the harm her magic might cause by mistake.

“I’m scared,” Elsa told her father one day. “It’s getting stronger.”

“Getting upset only makes it worse,” cautioned the king. “Calm down.” He reached out to give Elsa a hug.

“No,” she said sharply. “Don’t touch me.”

One day years later, when the girls were teenagers, the king and queen boarded a ship, intending to visit another kingdom. They hugged their daughters goodbye and left them at home, as they had many times before. But this time, the king and queen never returned. A storm engulfed the ship, and they were lost at sea. The kingdom mourned their rulers.

Inside the castle, Anna felt overcome with grief. Not knowing where else to turn, she knocked again on Elsa’s door.

“Elsa? Are you okay? I’m right out here,” Anna said. But as always, there was no reply. She slid down and sadly rested her head against the door. “It’s just you and me now. What are we going to do?”

Inside her room, Elsa felt awful, too. But she could not open the door. Instead, she sat with her back against the closed door, crying silently. All around her, ice and snow filled the room.

In time, the girls became young ladies. But they had grown apart, and Anna felt she barely knew Elsa anymore.

When Elsa turned twenty-one, it was time for her to be crowned the new Queen of Arendelle. The whole kingdom was bustling with excitement. For the first time in ages, and for one day only, the castle gates would be opened to the village and to all the surrounding kingdoms.

It would be a celebration that Arendelle would never forget.

chapters.title: 第四章 · 加冕之晨
chapters.en:
On the morning of Elsa’s coronation, the heavy gates to the castle were finally opened. All of Arendelle wanted to celebrate the grand occasion. The streets in front of the castle were crowded with townspeople eager to see the new queen.

To add to the excitement, the fjord was filled with ships from other kingdoms, bringing dignitaries from far away. One by one, important people stepped onto Arendelle’s docks.

“Welcome to our humble Arendelle,” the royal handler called to the visitors. One of the visiting dignitaries was the Duke of Weselton, a small man with white whiskers. Two huge guards followed close behind him, carrying his luggage.

“Ah, Arendelle, our most mysterious trade partner,” the Duke said breezily. “Open those gates so I may unlock your secrets and exploit your riches!”

In the distance, Kristoff was making his way down a mountain path. Now grown-up and strong, he and Sven had become true ice harvesters, masters at hauling ice blocks down the mountain. To Kristoff, the coronation was a perfect opportunity to sell ice to the crowds who filled Arendelle.

“A coronation on a hot July day, you know what that means?” he asked Sven, who was harnessed to their rickety ice cart.

The reindeer raised his eyebrows. Sven couldn’t talk, but that wasn’t a problem for Kristoff. He often spoke for Sven, changing his voice to sound deeper and more reindeer-y.

“I sure do, Kristoff,” he declared, as Sven. “By noon I’m going to smell like a barrel of rabid skunks.”

“Yes, you will,” Kristoff said, talking normally again. He grinned. “But also, people will be needing ice. Lots of ice.” He pulled Sven’s rope, and the two continued down into the town.

For Anna, the new people and the excitement were a dream come true. For the first time in years, every door in Arendelle was open. No one was shutting her out! She burst through the busy courtyard in front of the castle and practically skipped into town. People everywhere were getting ready for the coronation. She saw banners, a maypole, and flowers—all celebrating her sister, the new queen. There were dancing groups, musical bands, and food stalls. Everything looked so interesting.

“I can’t wait to meet everyone!” Anna exclaimed out loud. Then she stopped short as a thought occurred to her. “What if I meet the one?” Anna knew she wasn’t likely to meet someone special, especially since the castle gates would be open for one day only, exactly twenty-four hours. Still, she couldn’t help daydreaming just a bit. Today might be her only chance to meet new friends, have new experiences, and maybe, just maybe, find love.

In her room upstairs in the castle, Elsa did not share the happiness that pulsed through the kingdom. She worried about controlling her powers, and hoped she could just get through the ceremony without anyone learning about her magic.

As a test, she slipped off her gloves and picked up a candlestick and a little jar from the table. She concentrated, holding both with her bare hands. “Be the good girl,” Elsa whispered to herself. “Make one wrong move and everyone will know.…” She was nervous. As she stood there, ice formed on her palms and moved onto the objects, turning them to ice. She hurriedly dropped them and tugged her gloves back on, concealing her hands—and her icy magic.

“It’s only for today,” Elsa reminded herself. After that, the gates would be closed again and she could go back into hiding.
chapters.zh: 加冕典礼那天的清晨，城堡厚重的大门终于开启。 整个阿伦黛尔都盼着庆祝这一盛典。 城堡前的街道挤满了急欲一睹新女王风采的百姓。 更添热闹的是，峡湾里停满了来自其他王国的船只，远道而来的使节纷纷抵岸。 贵宾们逐一踏上阿伦黛尔的码头。「欢迎来到我们质朴的阿伦黛尔，」迎宾官向访客高声说道。 来访使节中有一位韦塞尔顿公爵，是个留着白胡子的小个子男人。 两名魁梧的侍卫紧随其后，替他搬运行李。「啊，阿伦黛尔，我们最神秘的贸易伙伴，」公爵轻飘飘地说，「打开大门吧，好让我揭开你们的秘密，榨取你们的财富！」远处，克斯托夫正沿着山道下行。 如今他已长大成人、身强体壮，和斯特成了真正的采冰人，熟练地将冰块从山上运下。 对克斯托夫而言，加冕礼正是向涌入阿伦黛尔的人潮售卖冰块的好时机。「七月酷暑里办加冕礼，你知道这意味着什么吗？」他问套着那辆破冰车的斯特。 驯鹿扬了扬眉。 斯特不会说话，可这对克斯托夫不算问题。 他常替斯特开口，故意压低嗓音，装出更「驯鹿」的腔调。「我当然知道，克斯托夫，」他模仿斯特宣布，「到中午我就会臭得像一桶发疯的臭鼬。」「没错，你会的，」克斯托夫恢复平常的语调说道。 他咧嘴一笑。「不过，人们也需要冰块。 大量的冰块。」他拉了拉斯特的缰绳，主仆二人继续向镇子走去。 对安娜来说，这些新面孔与喧腾景象，简直是美梦成真。 多年来头一回，阿伦黛尔的每一扇门都敞开着。 再没有人将她拒之门外！ 她冲过城堡前繁忙的庭院，几乎是蹦跳着进了城。 四处的人们都在为加冕礼做准备。 她看见旗帜、五朔节花柱与鲜花——全都在为她姐姐、新任女王庆祝。 有舞蹈队、乐队，还有各色小吃摊。 一切都那么有趣。「我等不及要认识大家了！」安娜大声感叹。 接着她猛地停住，一个念头掠过心头。「要是我遇见那个对的人呢？」安娜明白，自己遇见特别之人的机会微乎其微，尤其城堡大门只开启区区一天，整整二十四小时。 尽管如此，她还是忍不住稍稍做起了白日梦。 今天也许是她结交新友、体验新事，或许——只是或许——寻得爱情的唯一机会。 在城堡楼上的房间里，艾莎却无从分享举国欢腾的喜悦。 她忧心自己能否控制力量，只盼能挨过典礼，而不让任何人察觉她的魔法。 为了测试，她摘下手套，从桌上拿起一支烛台和一个小罐。 她凝神静气，用赤裸的双手捧住二者。「做个乖女孩，」艾莎对自己低语，「只要一步走错，大家就都知道了……」她紧张极了。 她站在那里，掌心凝出冰霜，顺着物体蔓延，将它们冻成了冰。 她慌忙放下它们，重新套回手套，藏起双手——也藏起冰雪魔法。「只是今天一天而已，」艾莎提醒自己。 之后，大门将再度紧闭，她便能重新躲回隐秘之中。

chapters.title: 第五章 · 海港的遐想
chapters.en:
In the streets below, Anna was strolling dreamily around the harbor, watching the ships and imagining all the fun the coronation party would bring. For once, it wouldn’t matter that Elsa didn’t want to spend time with her, because she’d be spending time with everyone else!

Anna rounded a corner and suddenly–smack!–a horse bumped into her!

Caught by surprise, Anna lost her balance and stumbled, falling into a small rowboat on the dock. The boat tipped precariously toward the water. Luckily, the horse came forward and placed its hoof on the end of the boat to keep it from sliding into the harbor.

“Hey!” Anna exclaimed in surprise, looking up at the horse and its rider.

“I’m so sorry,” the rider said. “Are you hurt?”

Anna tried to regain her composure. “Hey, uh… No, I’m okay,” she managed to say. She couldn’t help noticing that the rider was very handsome.

“Are you sure?” the young man asked. He hopped off his horse. He was tall and sharply dressed in a fancy uniform. He looked very concerned about her welfare.

“Yeah, I just wasn’t looking where I was going,” Anna said. She smiled. “But I’m great, actually.”

“Oh, thank goodness,” the stranger said, smiling. He stepped into the little boat and extended his hand to Anna. When their eyes met, a happy charge of excitement passed between them.

The young man smiled. “Prince Hans of the Southern Isles,” he said, introducing himself.

Anna stood up and curtsied. “Princess Anna of Arendelle,” she replied.

“Princess?” he responded, horrified. “My lady!” He dropped to one knee and bowed his head.

His horse also dropped to one knee. Immediately, the little boat tipped backward, and Hans tumbled on top of Anna. They both giggled awkwardly.

“Hi again,” Anna said. The prince’s face was just inches from hers.

Apparently realizing his mistake, the horse slammed its hoof back down on the boat. Anna and Hans fell the opposite way. This time, Anna landed on top of Hans!

“Oh, boy,” Hans said, embarrassed.

“Ha! This is awkward,” Anna said, acknowledging their positions. “Not that you’re awkward,” she said, trying to cover her embarrassment. “But just because we’re…I’m awkward!” she said. “You’re gorgeous.” Her hand flew to her mouth. Had she just said that out loud? “Wait, what?”

Hans jumped to his feet, quickly regaining a royal posture. “I’d like to formally apologize for hitting the Princess of Arendelle with my horse. And for every moment after,” he added.

“No, no,” Anna said. “It’s fine. I’m not that princess. I mean, if you’d hit my sister, Elsa, this would be…” She paused for a moment. “Yeesh! Because, you know…” Anna patted the horse, trying to recover her rambling thoughts. “Hello,” she said to the horse. She turned back to Hans and offered him a princess grin. “But lucky for you, it’s just me.”

“Just you?” Hans asked. A warm smile spread across his face.

Anna couldn’t help smiling back. All of sudden, the castle bells began to peal.

“The bells!” she cried. “The coronation—I’d better go,” she said. She hopped off the boat onto the pier and waved. “Uh, bye!”

Hans waved back. Even the horse waved, lifting his hoof off the boat for a moment. Unfortunately, that caused the boat’s weight to shift again.

“Oh, no!” Hans said.

The boat flipped off the dock and Hans fell into the water with a splash! Lifting the boat off his head, Hans peeked up from the water and watched Anna run through the streets toward the castle. He grinned as he thought about his wonderful chance meeting with the beautiful princess.

Soon the people of Arendelle, along with dignitaries from around the land, were making their way into the royal church for Elsa’s coronation. Kristoff, however, was far away, in a corner of the town. He had sold all his ice and was now busy bargaining for a brand-new sled.

“Watch this, Sven,” Kristoff called as he played around with the sled’s special features, which allowed it to switch between runners and wheels. “It’s a sled! It’s a wagon! It’s a sled! It’s a wagon!”

The sled salesman looked concerned, as if he was wondering what kind of person would talk to a reindeer. But he wanted to finish the sale. He tried to make small talk as they completed their deal. “You sticking around to see the queen and the princess?” he asked Kristoff.

“Are you kidding?” Kristoff replied. “I’ve got a brand-new sled…with wheels!” He grinned. “I’m hitting the road.”

“Suit yourself,” the man said. “But I bet they’re beautiful.”

Kristoff didn’t even hear the man. He and Sven were already headed back to the mountains with their new sled.
chapters.zh: 在下面的街道上，安娜正梦游般地在海港边闲逛，望着船只，想象着加冕典礼的宴会会带来多少欢乐。这一次，艾莎不愿陪她这件事总算不要紧了，因为她要和大家一起欢度！安娜转过一个街角，忽然——砰！——一匹马撞上了她！安娜猝不及防，失去平衡踉跄了一下，跌进了码头边的一艘小划艇里。小艇危险地朝水面倾斜过去。幸好那匹马走上前，把蹄子踩在小艇末端，不让它滑进海港。"嘿！"安娜又惊又喜地抬头看着马和骑马的人。"真对不起，"骑马的人说，"你受伤了吗？"安娜努力镇定下来。"嘿，呃……没有，我没事，"她好不容易说出话来。她忍不住注意到，这位骑手十分英俊。"你确定吗？"年轻人问。他跳下马。他身材高大，穿着笔挺华丽的制服。他看起来十分关切她的安危。"是啊，我只是没看路，"安娜说。她笑了："不过其实我好得很。""哦，谢天谢地，"陌生人微笑着说。他踏进小艇，向安娜伸出手。当四目相对，一股喜悦的悸动在两人之间流淌。年轻人微笑着自我介绍："南境群岛的汉斯王子。"安娜站起身行了个屈膝礼。"阿伦黛尔的安娜公主，"她答道。"公主？"他惊呼，随即单膝跪下低头行礼："我的 lady！"他的马也单膝跪下。立刻，小艇向后一翻，汉斯摔在了安娜身上。两人尴尬地咯咯笑起来。"又见面了，"安娜说。王子的脸离她只有几寸远。马显然意识到了自己的失误，猛地把蹄子踩回小艇上。安娜和汉斯朝相反方向倒去。这一次，安娜压在了汉斯身上！"哎呀，"汉斯尴尬地说。"哈！真尴尬，"安娜边说边意识到两人的姿势。"不是你尴尬，"她掩饰着自己的窘态，"是因为我们……是我自己尴尬！"她说，"你真好看。"手一下子捂住了嘴。她刚才是说出口了吗？"等等，什么？"汉斯一跃而起，迅速恢复了王子的仪态。"我要为我的马撞到阿伦黛尔公主正式道歉。也为之后发生的每一刻，"他补充道。"不不，"安娜说，"没关系。我不是那位公主。我是说，如果你撞的是我姐姐艾莎，那可就……"她顿了顿，"天哪！因为，你知道……"安娜拍了拍马，努力找回自己乱成一团的想法。"你好，"她对马说。她转回身对汉斯露出一个公主式的微笑。"不过你运气好，撞的只是我。""只是你？"汉斯问。他脸上绽开温暖的笑容。安娜忍不住也笑了。突然，城堡的钟声敲响了。"钟声！"她叫道，"加冕典礼——我得走了，"她说。她跳下小艇踏上码头挥手。"呃，再见！"汉斯也挥手道别。连那匹马也"挥"了挥——把蹄子从艇上抬起来了一瞬。不幸的是，这一下又让小艇重心偏移。"哦，不！"汉斯说。小艇翻出码头，汉斯扑通一声掉进了水里！汉斯把小艇从头上挪开，从水里探出头，望着安娜穿过街道朝城堡跑去。他咧嘴笑着，想着与那位美丽公主的美妙偶遇。不久，阿伦黛尔的民众连同各地的显贵，纷纷走进皇家教堂，参加艾莎的加冕典礼。然而，克斯托夫在很远的小镇角落里。他已经卖光了所有的冰，正忙着讨价还价买一辆崭新的雪橇。"看好了，斯文，"克斯托夫摆弄着雪橇的特殊功能——它能在滑橇和轮子之间切换——喊道。"这是雪橇！这是马车！这是雪橇！这是马车！"卖橇的商人一脸担忧，仿佛在琢磨什么样的人会对着驯鹿说话。但他还是想做成这笔买卖。成交时他试着闲聊："你留下来看女王和公主吗？"他问克斯托夫。"开什么玩笑？"克斯托夫答道，"我有一辆崭新的、带轮子的雪橇！"他咧嘴一笑，"我这就上路。""随你，"那人说，"不过我打赌她们一定很美。"克斯托夫根本没听进去。他和斯文已经带着新雪橇朝山区出发了。

chapters.title: 第六章 · 加冕典礼
chapters.en:
The cathedral was packed with people as the coronation ceremony began. An orchestra played and a choir sang while the royal procession walked down the very long center aisle. The bishop led the way, followed by Elsa, looking regal and serious, and finally Anna, holding the train of Elsa’s dress.

At the altar, Elsa and Anna faced the bishop. Near him lay a silver platter holding the royal crown, scepter, and orb.

Peeking over her shoulder, Anna spotted the handsome Prince Hans. He sat straight and tall, and a stranger was asleep on his shoulder! Hans waved at Anna, who giggled.

The bishop placed the crown on Elsa’s head. Then he turned for the scepter and orb and presented them to Elsa. She reached for the royal items, but the bishop cleared his throat. “Ahem. Your gloves, Your Majesty.”

Elsa took a sharp breath. If she took the gloves off, she might accidentally let out her icy magic. She hesitated, growing pale with worry.

Anna took that moment to look over at Hans and smile at him. She couldn’t wait to talk to him at the ball!

Elsa slowly removed her gloves and placed them on the satin pillow. With a deep breath, she took the orb and scepter into her hands. She turned to face the crowd.

“As the undoubted queen, protector of this dominion,” the bishop intoned, “keeper of the doctrine and government thereof from this day forward, I present to you Her Majesty…”

Elsa’s eyes widened as the scepter and orb began to freeze in her hands! She tried desperately to control her emotions. She was just so nervous!

“…Queen Elsa of Arendelle!” The bishop finished his decree.

The people in the church rose. “Queen Elsa of Arendelle!” they echoed.

Elsa quickly placed the orb and scepter back on the silver tray and grabbed her gloves. With a sigh of relief, she realized that no one had seen the ice on the orb or the scepter. She smiled at the cheering crowd. She had made it through the ceremony!

Later, at the coronation ball, Elsa and Anna stood side by side in a long receiving line at the entrance to the Great Hall. Elsa felt relaxed, almost content, now that the most difficult part of Coronation Day was over. Festive music filled the air as guests danced across the floor of the lavishly decorated ballroom.

“You look beautiful,” Elsa said to Anna.

“Thank you,” Anna said in surprise. A smile spread across her face. Her sister had actually spoken to her! “You look beautiful-er,” Anna replied. Then she realized how strange that had sounded and blurted out an explanation. “Not that you’re fuller. No. Just more beautiful!”

Elsa grinned. “Thank you.” Then she looked out at the crowded ballroom. “So this is what a party looks like?”

Anna nodded. “It’s warmer than I thought.”

“All the people, I guess,” Elsa said. “And what is that amazing smell?”

Both of them caught a whiff of a sweet aroma wafting across the room. “Chocolate!” they exclaimed at the same time. Then they looked at each other and started laughing.

Anna could hardly believe that Elsa was treating her so kindly. She was about to say more to her sister, but just then, a guest stepped up to be presented to the new queen and the princess. “The Duke of Weaseltown,” a royal attendant announced.

“Weselton,” the Duke corrected him. Then he bowed his head. “As your closest partner in trade, it seems only fitting that I offer you your first dance as queen.”

Elsa stiffened and clasped her gloved hands together. “Thank you,” she said. “But I don’t dance.”

The Duke looked offended, so Elsa quickly nudged Anna forward. “But my sister is a marvelous dancer.”

Anna was a little startled, but she allowed the Duke to lead her to the dance floor.

Unfortunately, the Duke was a horrible dancer. He couldn’t seem to take one step without crushing Anna’s toes. As he bobbed up and down, his toupee bounced back and forth on his head—and he never stopped talking.

“Bump-be-dump-bah! Look at me!” he crowed. “This certainly makes up for being shut out for twelve years for no reason. Do you know the reason?” he asked Anna. “No? Well, watch this: like a chicken with the face of a monkey, I fly!”

Anna cringed as the Duke danced around her like a dying peacock. Then she caught sight of Elsa watching from the side of the room, barely able to keep from laughing. Anna shot Elsa a number of “help me” looks, but there was no way out of it. She was forced to finish the dance, much to Elsa’s amusement.

After the dance, Anna limped back to Elsa. “Well, he was sprightly,” said the queen with a smile.

“Especially for a man in heels!” Anna replied. Both sisters giggled.

“Are you all right?” Elsa asked more gently.

Anna smiled. “I’ve never been better,” she said, glancing into Elsa’s eyes. “This is so nice. I wish it could be like this all the time.”

“Me too,” Elsa said wistfully. Then she caught herself and stiffened. “But it can’t.”

“Why not?” Anna asked, surprised at Elsa’s sudden change of attitude.

Elsa tensed. “Because it can’t,” she said firmly.

Anna’s felt all her old disappointment rushing back. “Excuse me,” she said. Elsa watched sadly as Anna walked away.
chapters.zh: 加冕典礼开始时，大教堂里挤满了人。管弦乐队奏乐，唱诗班吟唱，王室队伍沿着漫长的中央通道缓步前行。主教引领在前，身后跟着神情庄重威严的艾莎，最后是替艾莎提着裙裾的安娜。在圣坛前，艾莎和安娜面向主教。他身旁摆着一只银盘，上面放着王冠、权杖和宝球。安娜回头一瞥，认出了英俊的汉斯王子。他坐得笔直挺拔，而一个陌生人竟枕着他的肩膀睡着了！汉斯朝安娜挥手，安娜咯咯笑了起来。主教把王冠戴到艾莎头上。接着他转身为权杖和宝球，将它们呈给艾莎。她伸手去接，主教却清了清嗓子。"嗯哼。您的手套，陛下。"艾莎倒吸一口凉气。如果她脱下手套，就可能不小心释放出冰魔法。她迟疑了，担心得脸色发白。安娜趁这时望向汉斯，对他微微一笑。她等不及要在舞会上和他说话了！艾莎缓缓摘下手套，放在缎面软垫上。深吸一口气，她把宝球和权杖握在手中。她转身面向人群。"作为无可争议的女王、这片疆土的保护者，"主教庄严宣告，"自今日起教义与治权之守护者，我向诸位呈献陛下……"艾莎睁大眼睛——权杖和宝球竟开始在手中结冰！她拼命想控制住自己的情绪。她实在太紧张了！"……阿伦黛尔的艾莎女王！"主教念完了敕令。教堂里的人们起身回应："阿伦黛尔的艾莎女王！"艾莎迅速把宝球和权杖放回银盘，抓回自己的手套。她松了口气，意识到没人看到宝球和权杖上的冰。她向欢呼的人群微笑。她总算熬过了典礼！稍后，在加冕舞会上，艾莎和安娜并肩站在大殿入口的长长的迎宾队伍中。既然加冕日最艰难的部分已经过去，艾莎感到轻松，几乎有几分满足。节日乐曲飘荡在空气中，宾客在华丽的大舞厅地板上翩翩起舞。"你真美，"艾莎对安娜说。"谢谢，"安娜有些意外。笑容在她脸上漾开。姐姐居然主动跟她说话了！"你更美，"安娜答道。随即她意识到这话有多奇怪，慌忙解释："不是说我你更丰满。不。只是更漂亮！"艾莎笑了："谢谢。"然后她望向拥挤的舞厅："原来聚会就是这样？"安娜点头："比我想象的暖和。""大概是因为这么多人吧，"艾莎说，"那股奇妙香味是什么？"两人同时闻到一缕甜香飘过。"巧克力！"她们异口同声。然后她们相视而笑。安娜几乎不敢相信艾莎对她如此亲切。她正想对姐姐多说几句，这时一位宾客上前，被引荐给新女王和公主。"黄鼠狼镇的公爵，"侍从宣布。"是维塞尔顿，"公爵纠正道。接着他低下头："作为您最亲密的贸易伙伴，由我来邀您以女王之姿跳第一支舞，再合适不过。"艾莎身子一僵，双手交握着戴手套的手。"谢谢，"她说，"但我不会跳舞。"公爵面露不悦，艾莎连忙把安娜推上前："可我妹妹舞跳得极好。"安娜有些惊讶，但还是随公爵走向舞池。不幸的是，公爵舞跳得糟透了。他似乎每走一步都要踩到安娜的脚趾。他上下蹦跳时，假发在头上前后乱颠——而且他嘴一刻不停。"蹦跶蹦跶吧！看我！"他得意地叫，"被毫无理由地关在门外十二年，这下总算补偿回来了。你知道原因吗？"他问安娜。"不知道？那看好：像长了猴脸的鸡，我飞！"公爵像只垂死的孔雀在她身边乱舞，安娜直皱眉。这时她瞥见艾莎站在房间一角看着，差点没笑出声。安娜朝艾莎投去无数个"救命"的眼神，却脱身无术。她被迫跳完了整支舞，而艾莎看得乐不可支。舞毕，安娜一瘸一拐地回到艾莎身边。"嗯，他还挺活泼，"女王微笑着说。"尤其对一个穿高跟鞋的男人来说！"安娜答道。姐妹俩都咯咯笑起来。"你还好吗？"艾莎温和地问。安娜微笑："我从没这么好过，"她望进艾莎的眼睛，"这真好。真希望永远都这样。""我也是，"艾莎怅然地说。随即她回过神来，身子一僵："可不行。""为什么不行？"安娜对艾莎态度的突变感到惊讶。艾莎绷紧身体："就是不行，"她坚定地说。安娜只觉得旧日的失望涌上心头。"失陪，"她说。艾莎伤心地望着安娜走远。

chapters.title: 第七章 · 翩然相遇
chapters.en:
Anna pushed through the crowd of guests, and one of the dancers tripped into her, knocking her backward. Someone grabbed her by the arms before she hit the floor.

“Glad I caught you,” Hans said, smiling.

“Hans!” she said, surprised.

Hans lifted Anna back to her feet, and the two immediately were drawn into the dance. Hans was an excellent dancer, and Anna was happy to let him guide her around the ballroom, twirling her at just the right moments. She was amazed at how natural it felt.

After that, she and Hans walked and laughed and danced some more. One hour turned into many hours of them talking and enjoying each other’s company.

Finally, they took a break and strolled into the rose garden. Hans plucked a rose and placed it in Anna’s hair. As he did, he noticed the white streak running down the side of her head. “What’s this?”

Anna put her hand to her hair. “I was born with it,” she told him. “Although I dreamt I was kissed by a troll.”

“I like it,” Hans said.

On the balcony, they sat on a bench and Anna taught Hans how to eat a krumkake. “Just bite it. The whole thing!” she said. The pair laughed as the treat crumbled all over Hans’s face.

Hans told Anna about his family. “I have twelve older brothers,” he said. “Three of them pretended I was invisible…for two years.”

“That’s horrible,” Anna said.

“It’s what brothers do,” he replied with a shrug.

Anna smiled knowingly. “And sisters,” she added. “Elsa and I were really close when we were little. But then one day she just shut me out, and I never knew why.”

“I would never shut you out,” Hans said, gazing into Anna’s eyes.

Anna beamed. “Okay, can I just say something crazy?” she asked.

“I love crazy,” Hans said with a wide grin.

“All my life has been a series of doors in my face,” she said. “Then suddenly, I bump into you!” Anna explained that she felt like she’d been waiting her whole life to meet him. And Hans agreed. He felt the same way! Anna couldn’t believe her good fortune. At last, here was someone who understood her. Someone who was open to new experiences and people, exactly the way she was. Hans was sweet, kind, and fun. They spent the rest of the party together, dancing, laughing, and discussing their pasts—and their futures, too.

“Can I say something crazy?” Hans asked suddenly. “Will you marry me?”

Anna gasped. “Can I just—ooh. I mean, yes!” She was amazed that she and Hans had found each other. She just knew that they were meant to be.

“Elsa!” Anna called from across the ballroom. She pulled Hans toward her sister. “May I present Prince Hans of the Southern Isles,” she said formally.

“Your Majesty.” Hans greeted the queen with a deep bow.

Anna was beaming. “We would like—”

“—your blessing—” Hans continued.

“—of our marriage!” Anna finished breathlessly.

“Marriage?” Elsa asked. “I’m confused.”

“Well, we haven’t worked out all the details,” Anna said. “We’ll need a few days to plan the ceremony. Of course, we’ll have soup, roast, and ice cream…” Anna turned to Hans. “Would we live here?”

“Here?” Elsa asked.

“Absolutely!” Hans cried.

“What? No,” Elsa said.

“And we’ll invite all twelve of your brothers to stay here with us, and—” Anna stopped as Elsa put up her hand.

“Wait,” she said. “Slow down. Anna, no one’s brothers are staying here. No one is getting married.”

Anna’s mouth dropped open. “Wait, what?”

“I need to talk to you,” Elsa said sternly. “Alone.”

Anna linked her arm with Hans’s. “No,” she said. “Whatever you have to say, you can say to both of us.”

Elsa shook her head. “No.… You can’t marry a man you just met.”

Standing straighter, Anna spoke up. “You can if it’s true love.”

“What do you know about true love?” Elsa replied, scoffing at her sister’s naiveté.

“More than you,” Anna replied. “All you want is to be alone.”

Elsa took a deep breath. “You asked for my blessing, but my answer is no. Now, if you’ll excuse me,” she said, and started to move away.

“Your Majesty,” Hans said. “If I may—”

“No, you may not,” Elsa snapped. “And I think you should go.” She walked off and signaled to one of the guards. “The party is over. It’s time to close the gates.”

Anna ran after her. “Elsa! No!” She reached for her sister and grabbed her hand. As she tugged at her to stay, Elsa’s glove slipped off.

“Give me my glove!” Elsa exclaimed.

Anna held the glove up and away from Elsa. “No, listen to me,” she said, “I can’t live like this anymore!”

Elsa fought to gain control. “Then leave,” she finally said. She saw the hurt on Anna’s face. She turned to flee from the room.

“What did I ever do to you?” Anna cried.

“Enough, Anna!” Elsa ordered.

“Why do you shut me out?” Anna asked. “Why do you shut the world out? What are you so afraid of?”

“I said enough!” Elsa shouted, spinning around. As she did, ice shot from her bare hand, coating the floor of the ballroom and frothing up into icy plumes.

The music stopped abruptly and everyone turned to stare at Elsa in shock. She stared at her subjects, wishing with all her heart that she could take the magic back.

But it was too late. Sheets of ice covered the dance floor. The Great Hall fell into a chilly silence.

The Duke gasped. “Sorcery! I knew there was something going on here.”

“Elsa?” Anna called, but Elsa was already pushing through the doors and racing out of the room.
chapters.zh: 安娜从宾客人群中挤过去，一个跳舞的人绊到她，把她撞得往后一仰。有人在她摔倒前抓住了她的胳膊。"幸好接住了你，"汉斯微笑着说。"汉斯！"她又惊又喜。汉斯把安娜扶起身，两人立刻被卷入舞步之中。汉斯舞跳得极好，安娜乐意让他带着自己在舞厅里旋转，每个转身都恰到好处。她惊讶于这一切竟如此自然。之后，她和汉斯边走边笑，又跳了几支舞。一小时变成了一茬又一茬的谈笑与相伴。终于，他们歇了口气，漫步走进玫瑰园。汉斯摘下一朵玫瑰，别在安娜发间。就在这时，他注意到她鬓边那道白色发丝。"这是什么？"安娜抬手摸了摸头发。"我生来就有，"她告诉他，"虽然我梦见是被地精亲了一口。""我喜欢，"汉斯说。在阳台上，他们坐在长椅上，安娜教汉斯怎么吃脆饼。"直接咬。整块吃！"她说。点心碎屑掉了一汉斯一脸，两人笑作一团。汉斯向安娜讲起他的家人："我有十二个哥哥，"他说，"其中三个假装我是透明的……长达两年。""太可怕了，"安娜说。"兄弟们就这样，"他耸耸肩。安娜会心一笑："姐妹也是，"她补充，"小时候我和艾莎很亲近。可有一天她突然把我关在门外，我始终不知原因。""我绝不会把你关在门外，"汉斯凝视着安娜的眼睛说。安娜眉开眼笑："好，我能说句疯话吗？"她说。"我最爱疯话了，"汉斯咧嘴一笑。"我这一辈子，门总是当着我的面关上，"她说，"然后忽然，我撞上了你！"安娜说，她觉得仿佛等了一辈子才遇见他。汉斯也深以为然。他也是同样的感觉！安娜不敢相信自己如此幸运。终于，有人懂她了。一个像她一样，对新鲜事物和人都敞开怀抱的人。汉斯温柔、善良又风趣。余下的舞会时光他们都在一起，跳舞、欢笑，聊着过去——也聊未来。"我能说句疯话吗？"汉斯忽然问，"你愿意嫁给我吗？"安娜倒吸一口气："我能——噢。我是说，愿意！"她惊叹自己竟与汉斯相遇相知。她就是知道，他们注定是一对。"艾莎！"安娜隔着舞厅喊道。她把汉斯拉到姐姐面前："请允许我介绍南境群岛的汉斯王子，"她正式地说，"陛下。"汉斯深深鞠躬向女王致意。安娜容光焕发："我们想要——""——您的祝福——"汉斯接话，"——为我们证婚！"安娜气喘吁吁地收尾。"结婚？"艾莎问，"我糊涂了。""嗯，细节还没全定，"安娜说，"我们还需要几天筹备典礼。当然，会有汤、烤肉和冰淇淋……"安娜转向汉斯，"我们住这儿吗？""这儿？"艾莎问。"当然！"汉斯喊道。"什么？不行，"艾莎说，"我们还要邀请你十二个哥哥都来同住，还有——"安娜在艾莎抬手时住了口。"等等，"艾莎说，"慢点。安娜，谁的哥哥都不会住这儿。没人要结婚。"安娜张大了嘴："等等，什么？""我得跟你谈谈，"艾莎严厉地说，"单独谈。"安娜挽住汉斯的胳膊："不，"她说，"你要说的话，可以对我们俩说。"艾莎摇头："不……你不能嫁给你刚认识的人。"安娜挺直身子："如果是真爱就可以。""你懂什么真爱？"艾莎嗤笑妹妹的天真。"比你懂，"安娜答道，"你只想一个人待着。"艾莎深吸一口气："你们要我祝福，但我的答案是不。现在，失陪，"她说着转身要走。"陛下，"汉斯说，"请允许我——""不，不允许，"艾莎厉声道，"我想你该走了。"她走开，向一名卫兵示意："宴会结束了。该关大门了。"安娜追上去："艾莎！不！"她伸手抓住姐姐的手。她拉着姐姐想留住她，艾莎的手套却滑落了。"把手套还我！"艾莎叫道。安娜把手套举高，不还给艾莎。"不，听我说，"她说，"我再也过不了这种日子了！"艾莎努力克制："那就走吧，"她终于说。她看到了安娜脸上的伤痛。她转身要逃出房间。"我到底做过什么对不起你的事？"安娜喊道。"够了，安娜！"艾莎命令道。"你为什么把我关在门外？"安娜问，"你为什么把全世界都关在门外？你到底在怕什么？""我说够了！"艾莎转过身大喊。就在这时，冰从她裸露的手中射出，覆满了舞厅地板，又翻涌成冰柱。音乐骤然停止，所有人都转头震惊地盯着艾莎。她望着臣民，满心希望能让魔法收回。但为时已晚。整片冰层覆盖了舞池。大殿陷入一片冰冷的寂静。公爵倒吸凉气："妖术！我就知道这里不对劲。""艾莎？"安娜呼唤，可艾莎已经推开大门冲出了房间。

chapters.title: 第八章 · 秘密泄露
chapters.en:
Elsa burst into the courtyard. She was so afraid now that her secret was out. She hoped she hadn’t hurt anyone. Regardless, everyone in Arendelle would soon know about her magic.

“There she is!” cried a townswoman, excited to get a glimpse of the newly crowned queen. The woman obviously had no idea what had just happened in the ballroom. “Your Majesty! Long live the queen! Queen Elsa!”

Elsa backed away from the woman and quickly weaved through the crowd, trying hard not to touch anyone as she backed away. She didn’t want to cause any harm with her powers. She just wanted to leave the kingdom and hide!

A young woman with a small child in her arms called to her. “Your Majesty, are you all right?” she asked, full of concern.

Elsa put her hands behind her and moved away. She slowly walked backward, accidentally bumping into the fountain in the center of the courtyard. As soon as she touched the fountain, the water in it froze to solid ice.

There was a loud gasp from the villagers. People turned and ran away from Elsa.

The Duke and his guards ran down the castle steps. “There she is!” he shouted, leading the charge toward Elsa. “Get her!”

“Just stay away from me! Stay away!” Elsa cried. She held her hands up, causing the castle steps to ice over. The Duke’s guards slipped and tumbled down to the ground.

“Monster!” the Duke hissed.

The crowd panicked. A swirl of cold air traveled through Arendelle as Elsa ran along the streets, leaving ice and snow in her wake.

Anna watched from the castle gates. “Elsa!” she called. “Wait, please!” She rushed from the castle and ran after Elsa. Hans trailed behind her. “Elsa!” Anna cried desperately.

Elsa looked over her shoulder as she neared the water. When she turned, her foot touched the lapping waves—and the water in the fjord immediately froze. She took another cautious step…and another sheet of ice bloomed under her foot.

“Elsa!” Anna called after her.

Feeling her panic grow, Elsa ran across the fjord. With each step, more water froze underneath her. Soon she was moving at full speed, heading toward the mountains on the other side of the lake. As she passed, the ships belonging to the visiting dignitaries creaked and locked into place, frozen in the ice. The gorgeous summer day had turned into a growing winter storm.

“Elsa, stop!” Anna pleaded. She rushed onto the fjord after her sister but slipped on the ice. She was too far behind to catch up.

Hans reached out for Anna and helped her to stand. “Anna, are you all right?” he asked.

They both watched as Elsa reached the far shore and made her way into the mountains. Anna strained to see the path Elsa had taken.

“Did you know?” Hans asked Anna.

“No,” Anna replied. Then she nodded. “But it makes so much sense.”

They walked back through the village and overheard the Duke speaking. He was addressing a growing crowd of concerned people. “The queen has cursed this land,” he said. “She must be stopped! You must go after her!”

Anna rushed over to him. “No!” she shouted. “No one is to go anywhere.”

“You!” The Duke shook a finger at Anna. “Is there sorcery in you, too?” he shouted. “Are you a monster, too?”

“No, I’m completely ordinary,” Anna replied.

Hans took her hand. “That’s right, she is,” he told the Duke.

“And my sister is not a monster,” Anna added.

The Duke scowled. “She nearly killed me,” he said dramatically.

“You slipped on ice,” Hans pointed out.

Anna stepped forward. “It was an accident. She was scared. She didn’t mean it. She didn’t mean any of this.” She paused. “All she’s ever wanted is to be perfect and good. Tonight was my fault. I pushed her. So I’m the one who needs to go after her.”

Anna turned to her royal guards. “Bring me my horse, please.”

“What? Anna, no!” Hans shouted. “It’s too dangerous.”

“I’m not afraid of Elsa,” Anna said. “I’ll bring her back and make this right.”

A royal guard brought Anna’s horse to her. She took her cloak, which was hanging over the saddle, and wrapped it around her shoulders.

“I’m coming with you,” Hans said.

“No,” Anna told him. “I need you here to take care of Arendelle.”

Hans saw the desperation in Anna’s eyes. He put his hand to his chest. “On my honor,” he said, bowing his head.

“I leave Prince Hans in charge!” Anna told the crowd.

“Are you sure you can trust her?” Hans asked as Anna mounted the horse. When Anna didn’t reply, he leaned in. “I don’t want you getting hurt.”

“She’s my sister,” Anna said. “She’d never hurt me.”

Urging her horse into a gallop, Anna took off over the frozen fjord toward the mountains as snow continued to fall.

Elsa trudged up the steep North Mountain. Ever since she was a child, she had been taught to conceal her powers. Now that was all over. She felt sad and worried as she gazed back at Arendelle far below. She knew no one in Arendelle would ever see her in the same way again.

But a tiny part of her also felt relieved. Her magic had been a hard secret to keep, and she didn’t have to hide it anymore. Being alone was easier, too. She didn’t have to worry about hurting anyone.

As she continued up the mountain, her steps actually became a little lighter. Now that everyone knew what she was capable of, she was free to be herself!

With a wave of her hand, Elsa started to experiment with her magic. Snow and ice whirled around her as she created snowmen and icy patterns in the air. The farther she got from Arendelle, the more confident she felt. As she took each step, her ability to draw forth ice and cold grew stronger and more powerful.

Elsa plucked off her crown and threw it aside. She tossed her head and her tightly bound hair came loose, cascading over one shoulder in a thick, wavy braid. Twirling around, she conjured up a flowing new outfit of ice, a crystal-blue gown with a cape of gossamer frost. Snow was her element. She was the Snow Queen!

Thrilled to let her powers loose at last, Elsa found that she could do more than she realized. As released her magic, a staircase of ice extended upward…to an exquisite ice palace that grew as she raised her arms!

This was where she would live. When the castle was finished, Elsa slammed the door. She was home at last.

艾莎冲进了庭院。

秘密已经泄露，她此刻害怕极了。

她希望自己没有伤到任何人。

无论如何，阿伦黛尔的每个人很快都会知道她的魔法了。「她在那儿！」一位镇上女子喊道，兴奋地想一睹这位新加冕女王的风采。

这名女子显然对刚才在舞厅里发生的一切毫不知情。「陛下！

女王万岁！

艾莎女王！」艾莎从那女子身边退开，迅速穿梭在人群中，一边后退一边极力避免碰到任何人。

她不想用自己的力量造成任何伤害。

她只想离开王国，躲藏起来！

一位怀里抱着小孩子的年轻女子朝她喊道。「陛下，您还好吗？」她关切地问道。

艾莎把双手背到身后，移开了。

她缓缓地向后退去，不小心撞上了庭院中央的喷泉。

她的手一碰到喷泉，里面的水就冻成了坚冰。

村民们发出一阵惊呼。

人们转过身，从艾莎身边跑开。

韦斯文顿�公爵和他的卫兵冲下城堡台阶。「她在那儿！」他喊着，带头朝艾莎冲去。「抓住她！」「离我远点！

离我远点！」艾莎哭喊道。

她举起双手，城堡的台阶瞬间结上了一层冰。

韦斯文顿�公爵的卫兵脚下一滑，跌跌撞撞地滚落到地上。「怪物！」韦斯文顿�公爵咬牙切齿地说。

人群恐慌起来。

艾莎沿着街道奔跑，所到之处留下冰雪，一股寒风旋流席卷了整个阿伦黛尔。

安娜从城堡大门望去。「艾莎！」她喊道，「等等，求你了！」她冲出城堡，去追艾莎。

汉斯跟在她身后。「艾莎！」安娜绝望地喊道。

艾莎临近水边时，回头望了一眼。

她转过身，脚尖触到了拍岸的波浪——峡湾里的水顿时冻结了。

她又谨慎地迈出一步……脚下又绽放出一片坚冰。「艾莎！」安娜在她身后喊道。

艾莎感到恐慌愈发强烈，便奔跑着越过峡湾。

她每迈出一步，脚下就有更多的水冻结。

很快，她全速奔跑起来，朝湖对面的群山奔去。

她经过时，来访使节们的船只吱嘎作响，被冻在冰里，牢牢固定住。

美好的夏日已演变成一场愈演愈烈的冬日风暴。「艾莎，停下！」安娜恳求道。

她冲上峡湾去追姐姐，却在冰面上滑倒了。

她落后太远，追不上了。

汉斯伸手扶住安娜，帮她站起身。「安娜，你还好吗？」他问道。

两人望着艾莎抵达对岸，走向群山之中。

安娜费力地想看清艾莎离去的路。「你早就知道吗？」汉斯问安娜。「不知道，」安娜答道。

接着她点了点头。「但这太说得通了。」她们穿过村庄往回走，无意间听到韦斯文顿�公爵正在讲话。

他正对一群越来越多、忧心忡忡的人讲话。「女王诅咒了这片土地，」他说，「必须阻止她！

你们必须去追她！」安娜冲到他面前。「不！」她喊道，「谁也不准去任何地方。」「你！」韦斯文顿�公爵朝安娜晃着手指。「你身上也有妖术吗？」他喊道，「你也是怪物吗？」「不，我普普通通，」安娜答道。

汉斯握住她的手。「没错，她就是普通人，」他对韦斯文顿�公爵说。「而且我姐姐不是怪物，」安娜补充道。

韦斯文顿�公爵沉着脸。「她差点害死我，」他夸张地说。「你是踩在冰上滑倒了，」汉斯指出。

安娜走上前。「那是个意外。

她当时吓坏了。

她不是故意的。

这些事她一样也不是故意的。」她顿了顿。「她一直想要的，不过是做到完美、做个好人。

今晚是我的错。

是我逼她的。

所以应该由我去追她。」安娜转向她的皇家卫兵。「请把我的马牵来。」「什么？

安娜，不行！」汉斯喊道，「太危险了。」「我不怕艾莎，」安娜说，「我会把她带回来，把一切纠正过来。」一名皇家卫兵把安娜的马牵了过来。

她拿起搭在马鞍上的斗篷，裹在肩上。「我要跟你一起去，」汉斯说。「不行，」安娜告诉他，「我需要你留在这里照看阿伦黛尔。」汉斯看出了安娜眼中的绝望。

他把手按在胸口。「以我的名誉起誓，」他低头说道。「我任命汉斯代为摄政！」安娜对人群宣布。安娜上马时，汉斯问：「你确定能信任她吗？

安娜没有回答，他凑近了些。「我不想你受到伤害。」「她是我姐姐，」安娜说，「她绝不会伤害我。」安娜催马飞奔，在依旧飘落的雪花中，越过冰封的峡湾，朝群山而去。

艾莎艰难地爬上陡峭的北山。

从孩提时起，她就一直被教导要掩藏自己的力量。

而如今，这一切都结束了。

她回望脚下远处的阿伦黛尔，心中充满悲伤与忧虑。

她知道，阿伦黛尔再也不会有人用从前那样的眼光看她了。

但她心底也有一小部分感到如释重负。

她的魔法曾是个难以保守的秘密，而现在她不必再隐藏它了。

独自一人，反而也更轻松。

她不必再担心会伤到任何人。

随着她继续向山上走去，脚步竟真的变得轻快了些。

既然大家都已知道她能做到什么，她便可以自由地做自己了！

艾莎挥了挥手，开始尝试运用自己的魔法。

冰雪在她周身盘旋飞舞，她在空中变出雪人和冰晶图案。

离阿伦黛尔越远，她便越发自信。

随着她迈出的每一步，她汲取冰雪与严寒的能力也愈发强大。

艾莎摘下王冠，甩到一旁。

她甩了甩头，紧紧束起的头发松散开来，如一束浓密卷曲的发辫垂落在一侧肩头。

她旋转着身姿，变出一套飘逸的冰雪新装——一件水晶蓝的长裙，披着薄纱般的霜花斗篷。

冰雪，正是她的本元。

她就是冰雪女王！

终于得以尽情释放力量，艾莎兴奋地发现，自己能做到的比想象中更多。

随着她释放魔法，一道冰制阶梯向上延伸……通向一座精美的冰宫，随着她抬起双臂，冰宫不断生长！

这里，将是她栖身之所。

冰宫落成时，艾莎砰地关上了大门。

她终于到家了。

chapters.title: 第九章 · 风雪寻姐
chapters.en:
The wind howled and the snow blew into Anna’s face. She struggled to guide her horse up the frozen mountain path. She was determined to find Elsa. Anna was sure her sister would thaw the fjord and bring back summer. The whole kingdom would celebrate, and the two sisters would live happily ever after. The thought encouraged Anna as she rode through the snowdrifts.

“Elsa!” Anna called into the blizzard. “It’s me, Anna. Your sister who didn’t mean to make you freeze the summer!” She paused, shivering in the cold. “Wow, that’s a sentence I never thought I’d say. Anyway, I’m sorry! This is all my f-f-f-fault.”

A wolf’s howl interrupted Anna’s cries.

Her horse stopped and looked around nervously. Anna tried to convince herself that the sounds were just puppies playing.

“Of course, none of this would have happened if she’d just told me her secret,” Anna said with a sigh.

A tree branch snapped, and the horse panicked. It whinnied and kicked up its front legs.

“Whoa, whoa!” Anna commanded, pulling back on the reins. She flew off the horse into a snowdrift! She sat up, spit snow out of her mouth, and looked around just in time to see her horse running away.

“No, no, no! Come back!” Anna called, but the horse was long gone. “Okay,” she said to herself. She had to keep focused. She struggled to stand up and dusted the snow off her dress.

“Snow, it had to be snow,” she grumbled. “She couldn’t have had a tropical magic that covered the fjords in white sand and warm…” A welcome sight interrupted Anna’s rant. She saw smoke rising in the distance. “Fire!”

Anna took one more step and stumbled down a steep hill. She began to roll like a snowball, layering on more and more snow as she went.

Anna landed with a splash in an icy stream and the snowball broke apart. She got to her feet, shivering. “Cold, cold, cold, cold, cold…,” she muttered. She was standing next to a small building. A wooden sign hung in front of her: WANDERING OAKEN’S TRADING POST. A lump of snow fell off the sign. “And sauna!” she said, reading the end of the sign.

Anna hurried inside. The little shop was stocked with summer supplies—after all, it was technically still summertime. She gazed at the goods, looking for warm clothes.

“Hoo, hoo!” called a blond man behind the counter wearing a bright sweater. His name was Oaken, and he was the owner. “Big summer blowout,” he said hopefully. “Half off on our swimming suits, clogs, and a sun balm of my own invention, ja?”

“Oh, great,” Anna said, looking around the store. “For now, how about boots? Winter boots and dresses?”

“Well, that would be in our winter department,” the man said in a thick accent.

Anna darted toward the single rack of warm clothing. “Oh, um, I was just wondering,” she said, trying to sound casual, “has another young woman, the queen, perhaps, I don’t know, passed through here?” She brought a pair of boots and some clothes to the counter and set them in front of Oaken.

“Only one crazy enough to be out in the storm is you, dear,” Oaken said in a pleasant voice.

At that moment, the front door opened and a gust of frigid air blew in. A large, broad man entered. He was dressed for the arctic cold and completely covered in snow, with only his brown eyes showing. It was Kristoff, and he was looking for supplies, too.

“You and this fellow. Hoo, hoo,” Oaken sang out. “Big summer blowout.”

Kristoff pushed past Oaken and went straight to Anna. “Carrots,” he demanded.

“Huh?” Anna asked.

“Behind you,” Kristoff said crossly, pointing.

“Oh, right,” Anna said. “Excuse me.” She moved out of the way, and Kristoff grabbed a bag of carrots from a shelf behind her. He gathered a few other supplies as he moved briskly around the shop.

“A real howler in July, ja?” Oaken said, trying to make conversation with the stranger. “Wherever could it be coming from?”

“The North Mountain,” Kristoff replied.

“The North Mountain,” Anna repeated to herself. Was that where Elsa had gone?

风呼啸着，雪花扑打在安娜脸上。

她费力地指引马儿走上冰冻的山路。

她下定决心要找到艾莎。

安娜坚信姐姐会融化峡湾，让夏天回来。

整个王国都会欢庆，两姐妹也会从此幸福地生活下去。

这个念头鼓舞着安娜，她骑着马穿过雪堆。「艾莎！」安娜在暴风雪中喊道，「是我，安娜。

你那个并非故意让你把夏天冻住的妹妹！」她顿了顿，在寒冷中瑟瑟发抖。「哇，这话我可从没想过自己会说出口。

总之，对不起！

这都是我的错——错——错——错。」一声狼嚎打断了安娜的呼喊。

她的马停下脚步，紧张地四处张望。

安娜努力说服自己，那声音只是小狗在玩耍。「当然，要是她当初把秘密告诉我，这一切都不会发生，」安娜叹了口气说。

一根树枝咔嚓折断，马儿惊慌起来。

它嘶鸣着，前蹄腾空。「吁，吁！」安娜勒紧缰绳，大声喝止。

她从马上飞了出去，跌进一个雪堆！

她坐起身，把嘴里的雪吐出来，环顾四周，正好看见她的马跑远了。「不，不，不！

回来！」安娜喊道，可马早已跑得不见踪影。「好吧，」她对自己说。

她得保持专注。

她挣扎着站起来，拍掉裙子上的雪。「偏要是雪，偏偏是雪，」她嘟囔着，「她怎么就不能有种热带魔法，用白沙和暖意盖住峡湾……」一个令人欣喜的景象打断了安娜的牢骚。

她看见远处升起了炊烟。「火！」安娜又迈出一步，却顺着陡峭的山坡跌了下去。

她像雪球一样滚了起来，沿途裹上越来越多的雪。

安娜扑通一声落进一条冰冷的溪水，雪球随之散开。

她站起身，浑身发抖。「冷，冷，冷，冷，冷……」她喃喃自语。

她站在一间小屋旁。

一块木招牌挂在她面前：流浪奥肯杂货铺。

一团雪从招牌上掉落。「还有桑拿房！」她读着招牌末尾，说道。

安娜匆匆走了进去。

小店里备满了夏日用品——毕竟，严格来说现在还是夏天。

她盯着货物，寻找保暖的衣物。「嗬，嗬！」柜台后一个身穿亮色毛衣的金发男子招呼道。

他叫奥肯，是店主人。「夏日大甩卖，」他满怀期待地说，「泳衣、木屐，还有我自创的防晒膏，通通半价，是吧？」「哦，太好了，」安娜环顾店里说，「不过现在嘛，先来双靴子怎么样？

冬靴和裙子？」「嗯，那得去我们的冬季专区，」那男子带着浓重的口音说。

安娜快步走向仅有的那排保暖衣物。「哦，嗯，我只是好奇，」她故作随意地说，「有没有另一位年轻女子，也许是女王，我也不知道，有没有从这里经过？」她拿了一双靴子和几件衣服到柜台，摆在奥肯面前。「亲爱的，敢在暴风雪里出来的疯子，只有你一个，」奥肯和颜悦色地说。

就在这时，前门开了，一阵刺骨的寒风灌了进来。

一个魁梧壮硕的男子走了进来。

他一身御寒装扮，浑身覆满白雪，只露出一双棕色的眼睛。

那是克斯托夫，他也是来采购物资的。「你和这位老兄。

嗬，嗬，」奥肯高声说，「夏日大甩卖。」克斯托夫推开元肯，径直走向安娜。「胡萝卜，」他索取道。「啊？」安娜问。「你身后，」克斯托夫没好气地指着说。「哦，对，」安娜说，「借过。」她让开身子，克斯托夫便从她身后的架子上抓了一袋胡萝卜。

他在店里利落地走动，又收了几样物资。「七月里这场呼啸大风，真是少见，是吧？」奥肯想和这个陌生人搭话，「到底是从哪儿刮来的呢？」「北山，」克斯托夫答道。「北山，」安娜在心里重复了一遍。

艾莎是不是去了那里？

chapters.title: 第十章 · 杂货店风波
chapters.en:
Kristoff brought his pile of supplies to the front counter.

“That’ll be forty, ja?” Oaken said.

“Forty?” Kristoff barked. “No, ten.”

“No, see, these are from our winter stock,” Oaken told him. “Where supply and demand have a big problem.”

“You want to talk about a supply-and-demand problem?” Kristoff asked. “I sell ice for a living!”

Anna walked over to the counter and smiled at Kristoff. “Ice. Really?” she said. “That’s a rough business to be in right now.”

“Forty,” Oaken repeated. “But I will throw in a visit to Oaken’s sauna. Hoo, hoo!”

Kristoff and Anna both peered over Oaken’s shoulder to see a family waving from a toasty sauna in a room behind him.

“Ten’s all I got,” Kristoff told him. “Help me out, ja?”

Oaken held up the bag of carrots. “Ten will get you this and no more.”

Kristoff glared at Oaken, seething.

“Just tell me one thing,” Anna said, moving closer to Kristoff. “What was happening on the North Mountain? Did it seem…magical?”

Kristoff pulled down his scarf, revealing his face. He looked down sharply at Anna. “Yes!” he shouted. “Now back up while I deal with this crook here.”

Oaken rose from his chair. He did not appreciate being called a crook. “What did you call me?” he said. He was much taller and wider than Kristoff had expected. Oaken loomed over the counter. Then, with a frown, Oaken swiftly threw Kristoff out of the shop.

Kristoff went flying out the door and landed face-first in a mound of snow next to Sven, who had been waiting patiently outside. Kristoff pulled his head out of the snow. “Ow!” he moaned.

“Goodbye!” Oaken said pleasantly, and slammed the door.

The reindeer snorted and moved over to Kristoff, snuffling and searching in the snow.

“No, Sven,” Kristoff told him. “I didn’t get your carrots.”

The hungry reindeer huffed in his face. Then Kristoff turned his head and spotted something that made him brighten. There was a barn behind the trading post—a warm place to spend the night.

“But I did find us a place to sleep,” he added. “And it’s free.”

Back in the shop, Oaken returned to his other customer. “I’m sorry about this violence,” he told Anna. “I will add a quart of lutefisk so we have good feelings.” He looked over at what she had selected. “Just the outfit and the boots, ja?”

Anna looked at her supplies, and then over at the bag Kristoff had left on the counter. She smiled as an idea occurred to her.

Shortly afterward, Anna left Oaken’s shop and looked around. She could hear singing coming from the barn. She pushed open the door quietly and peered inside. Kristoff was lying against a bale of hay, playing his lute. He was singing to his reindeer…and then, singing as Sven, he finished the song from the reindeer’s point of view.

“Ahem.” Anna cleared her throat. When Kristoff looked over, she smiled. “Nice duet,” she said.

“Oh, it’s just you,” he said when he saw Anna standing in front of him. “What do you want?”

“I want you to take me up the North Mountain,” she declared.

“I don’t take people places,” Kristoff replied. He closed his eyes and lay back in the hay.

“Let me rephrase that,” Anna said. She threw the sack of supplies she had just bought over to Kristoff. They were exactly the items he’d wanted.

“Umph!” he grunted as the heavy bag landed on his chest.

“Take me up the North Mountain,” she ordered.

Kristoff regarded her carefully. He was not used to taking orders. And he especially couldn’t see any reason to follow Anna’s.

“Look,” Anna said. “I know how to stop this winter.”

Kristoff hesitated. If the cold weather stopped, he might be able to sell his ice down in Arendelle again.

“We leave at dawn,” he said finally. “And you forgot the carrots for Sven.”

Anna dropped a bag of carrots on Kristoff’s face.

“Ooh!” he said.

“Oops, sorry, sorry,” Anna said. Then she caught herself. She was trying to take charge, after all. “We leave now,” she declared. “Right now!”

Kristoff looked over at Sven and offered him a carrot. Sven took a healthy bite. So did Kristoff. They looked at the stranger before them as they chewed. They both knew she had no clue what was ahead.

嗬，嗬！」克斯托夫和安娜都从奥肯肩头望去，看见他身后房间里一家人在暖融融的桑拿房里朝他们挥手。「我只有十块，」克斯托夫对他说，「帮帮忙，是吧？」奥肯举起那袋胡萝卜。「十块就只能买这个，别的免谈。」克斯托夫怒视奥肯，气得冒火。「只要告诉我一件事，」安娜说着，凑近克斯托夫，「北山上到底发生了什么？

看起来……像有魔法？」克斯托夫拉下围巾，露出了脸。

他锐利地低头盯着安娜。「没错！」他喊道，「现在退后，让我来对付这个骗子。」奥肯从椅子上站了起来。

他可不喜欢被人叫骗子。「你叫我什么？」他说。

他比克斯托夫预想的要高大魁梧得多。

奥肯在柜台上方居高临下地俯视着。

接着，奥肯皱起眉头，一把将克斯托夫扔出了店外。

克斯托夫飞出门外，脸朝下摔在斯文旁边的一堆雪里——斯文一直耐心地等在外面。

克斯托夫把头从雪里拔出来。「哎哟！」他呻吟道。「再见！」奥肯和和气气地说，砰地关上了门。

驯鹿喷了喷鼻息，凑到克斯托夫跟前，在雪里嗅来嗅去。「别找了，斯文，」克斯托夫对它说，「我没拿到你的胡萝卜。」饥肠辘辘的驯鹿冲他的脸喷了口气。

这时克斯托夫转过头，瞥见一样东西，顿时来了精神。

杂货铺后面有一间谷仓——一个过夜的暖和地方。「不过我倒是给咱们找着睡觉的地方了，」他补充道，「而且免费。」回到店里，奥肯回到另一位顾客身边。「这场打搅真不好意思，」他对安娜说，「我再添一夸脱腌鳕鱼，咱们就言归于好啦。」他看了看安娜挑的东西。「就这套衣服和这双靴子，是吧？」安娜看了看自己的物资，又瞥了一眼克斯托夫落在柜台上的袋子。

她笑了，心里冒出了一个主意。

不久，安娜离开奥肯的店，四下张望。

她听见谷仓里传来歌声。

她轻轻推开门，朝里面望去。

克斯托夫正靠在一捆干草上，弹着他的鲁特琴。

他在对驯鹿唱歌……接着，他模仿斯文的口吻，从驯鹿的视角把歌给唱完了。「咳咳。」安娜清了清嗓子。

克斯托夫抬头一看，她笑了。「不错的二重唱，」她说。「哦，原来是你，」他看到安娜站在面前，说道，「你想干什么？」「我要你带我上北山，」她宣称。「我可不载人去哪儿，」克斯托夫答道。

他闭上眼睛，躺回干草里。「那我换个说法，」安娜说。

她把刚买的那袋物资扔给克斯托夫。

那正是他想要的东西。「唔！」沉重的袋子砸在他胸口，他闷哼一声。「带我上北山，」她命令道。

克斯托夫仔细打量着她。

他可不习惯听人指挥。

更何况，他实在想不出有什么理由要听安娜的。「听着，」安娜说，「我知道怎么让这个冬天停下来。」克斯托夫犹豫了。

要是寒冷天气停了，他或许就能回阿伦黛尔卖冰了。「我们天亮出发，」他终于说，「还有，你忘了给斯文带胡萝卜。」安娜把一袋胡萝卜丢在克斯托夫脸上。「噢！」他说。「哎呀，对不起对不起，」安娜说。

接着她停住了自己。

毕竟，她正努力当家作主呢。「我们现在就走，」她宣布，「马上走！」克斯托夫看向斯文，递给它一根胡萝卜。

斯文痛快地咬了一大口。

克斯托夫也咬了一口。

两人嚼着东西，打量着面前的陌生人。

他们心里都清楚，她根本不知道前方等着她的是什么。

chapters.title: 第十一章 · 雪原疾驰
chapters.en:
Kristoff held the reins tightly, steering Sven and the sled through the thick, heavy snow. The night sky was cloudy with the promise of still more snow.

“Hang on!” Kristoff yelled to his passenger. “We like to go fast!”

Sven responded happily and charged forward through the drifts.

“I like fast,” Anna answered. She leaned back and put her feet up on the front of the sled to show that she was not bothered by the high speed.

“Get your feet down,” Kristoff scoffed. “This is fresh lacquer.” He glanced at her sideways. “Seriously, were you raised in a barn?” He leaned over and wiped down his new sled.

“No, I was raised in a castle,” Anna replied.

“So tell me,” Kristoff said, “what made the queen go all ice crazy?”

“It was all my fault,” Anna blurted out. “I got engaged and she freaked out, because I’d only just met him, you know, that day. And she said she wouldn’t bless the marriage.”

“Wait,” Kristoff said. “You got engaged to someone you just met that day?”

“Yeah, anyway,” Anna replied, dismissing his comment. “I got mad and yelled at her, and she tried to walk away, but I grabbed her glove, and—”

“Wait. You got engaged to someone you just met that day?” Kristoff repeated.

“Yes, are you listening?” Anna snapped. “Thing is, she wore the gloves all the time, but I just thought the girl’s got a thing about dirt.”

“Didn’t your parents ever warn you about strangers?” Kristoff asked.

“Yes, they did,” Anna said. She looked Kristoff over carefully and slid farther away from him on the seat. After all, he was a stranger. “But Hans is not a stranger.”

Kristoff raised his eyebrows. “Oh, yeah? What’s his last name?”

Anna frowned, thinking. “Of the Southern Isles?” she offered.

“What’s his favorite food?” Kristoff fired off.

Anna hesitated. “Sandwiches.”

“Best friend’s name?” Kristoff quickly followed up.

“Probably John,” Anna replied, reflecting that lots of people were named John. So maybe Hans’s best friend would be, too.

“Eye color?” Kristoff pressed.

“Dreamy.” Anna smiled.

“Have you had a meal with him yet?” Kristoff asked. “What if you hate the way he eats? What if you hate the way he picks his nose?”

Anna wrinkled her forehead. “Picks his nose?”

“And eats it,” Kristoff added.

“Excuse me, sir,” Anna said. “He is a prince.”

Kristoff shook his head. “All men do it.”

“Ewww!” Anna made a face. “Look, it doesn’t matter. It’s true love.”

“Doesn’t sound like true love,” Kristoff said, staring straight ahead.

“Are you some sort of love expert?” Anna asked.

“No, but I have friends who are,” he responded.

“You have friends who are love experts?” Anna asked sarcastically.

Kristoff’s eyes widened and he stopped the sled. “Stop talking,” he demanded.

“No, I want to meet these friends,” she insisted with a grin.

Kristoff put his hand over Anna’s mouth. “I mean it. Shhhh!” He stood up and looked into the dark woods. He held up a lantern. Suddenly, he yelled, “Sven! Go! GO!”

The sled took off and Anna fell backward. She saw glowing eyes in the darkness all around them. “What are they?” she whispered.

“Wolves,” Kristoff said.

“What do we do?” Anna asked. She looked at Kristoff and readied herself.

“I’ve got this,” Kristoff said calmly. “You just don’t fall off—and don’t get eaten.”

“But I want to help,” Anna said.

“No,” Kristoff replied.

“Why not?” Anna pouted.

“Because I don’t trust your judgment,” Kristoff said.

Anna was offended. “Excuse me?”

A wolf jumped at the sleigh, and Kristoff kicked it back. “Who marries a man she’s just met?”

Anna was seething. “It’s true love!” She picked up Kristoff’s lute and swung it at his head. He ducked, and Anna struck a wolf that was about to lunge onto the sled!

“Whoa!” Kristoff exclaimed, just as another wolf jumped up and knocked him down. He fell out and was dragged behind the sled.

“Christopher!” Anna cried.

“It’s Kristoff!” he yelled.

Anna took the lantern and lit the sled’s blanket on fire. She threw the flaming blanket toward Kristoff, and the wolves tumbled off him. Then she reached out and pulled him back onto the sled. Kristoff looked at her in dismay.

“You almost set me on fire,” he said.

“But I didn’t,” Anna replied.

Sven suddenly whinnied. Ahead of him was a steep drop into a massive gorge.

“Get ready to jump, Sven!” Anna called.

“You don’t tell him what to do!” Kristoff shouted. “I do!”

In one swift movement, he grabbed Anna and threw her onto Sven’s back. Then he unhooked the reindeer’s harness. “Jump!”

Sven leaped and cleared the gorge with Anna on his back.

Just behind them, Kristoff boldly jumped with the sled. The sled didn’t make it all the way across, but just before it fell into the gorge, Kristoff threw himself off and caught the edge of the cliff on the other side. Down below, his new sled burst into flames as he dangled from the cliff. “I just got it.” He looked down with a sigh. Then his hands started to slip on the slick ice. “Uh-oh,” he said in alarm. “No, no, no!”

Out of nowhere, an ax slammed into the snow just inches from his face. He heard Anna’s voice from above.

“Grab on!” she yelled.

The ax was attached to a rope that was secured around Sven.

“Pull, Sven!” Anna ordered.

Sven heaved and walked backward, lifting Kristoff to safety.

Anna and Kristoff peered over the edge at the burning sled. “I’ll replace your sled and everything in it,” she promised. She looked sadly at Kristoff. “And I understand if you don’t want to help me anymore.”

Kristoff watched as Anna walked away. Sven nuzzled him softly with his cold nose.

“Of course I don’t want to help her anymore,” he told the reindeer. “In fact, this whole thing has ruined me for helping anyone ever again.” He watched as Anna turned and started to walk in the opposite direction.

“But she’ll die on her own,” he said, speaking in Sven’s deep voice.

Kristoff looked away. “I can live with that,” he said.

Anna turned this way and that, unsure which way to go.

“But you won’t get your new sled if she’s dead,” Kristoff continued in Sven’s voice.

He sighed. “Wait up,” he called to Anna in his normal voice. “We’re coming.”

Anna grinned. “You are?” she said happily. Then she composed herself. “I mean, sure, I’ll let you tag along.”

Anna wasn’t sure what lay ahead, but she was very glad that Kristoff and Sven were coming with her.

克斯托夫紧紧握住缰绳，驾着斯文和雪橇穿过厚重的大雪。

夜空阴云密布，似乎还要下更多的雪。「抓紧了！」克斯托夫对坐雪橇的人喊道，「我们喜欢飞驰！」斯文欢快地应了一声，冲开积雪向前奔去。「我喜欢快，」安娜回答。

她向后一靠，把脚翘到雪橇前缘上，表明她丝毫没有被这高速吓到。「把脚放下去，」克斯托夫不屑地说，「这可是刚上的漆。」他斜眼瞥了她一下。「说真的，你是在谷仓里长大的吗？」他俯身擦了擦自己的新雪橇。「不，我是在城堡里长大的，」安娜答道。「那告诉我，」克斯托夫说，「女王怎么突然就冰雪发疯了？」「都是我的错，」安娜脱口而出，「我订婚了，她就崩溃了，因为我那天才刚认识他。」

「而且她说她不会祝福这桩婚事。」「等等，」克斯托夫说，「你跟一个当天才认识的人订婚了？」「是啊，总之，」安娜不理会他的话，答道，「我气坏了，冲她大喊，她想走开，可我抓住了她的手套，然后——」「等等。」

「你跟一个当天才认识的人订婚了？」克斯托夫重复道。「对，你有在听吗？」安娜没好气地说，「问题是，她一直戴着那副手套，可我还以为那姑娘就是有点洁癖。」「你父母从没提醒过你提防陌生人吗？」克斯托夫问。「提醒过，他们确实提醒过，」安娜说。

她仔细打量着克斯托夫，在座位上往离他更远的地方挪了挪。

毕竟，他是个陌生人。「可汉斯不是陌生人。」克斯托夫扬起眉毛。「哦，是吗？」

「他姓什么？」安娜皱起眉头想了想。「南方群岛的？」她试探着说。「他最喜欢吃什么？」克斯托夫连珠炮似的追问。

安娜犹豫了。「三明治。」「最好朋友叫什么？」克斯托夫紧跟着问。「大概是约翰吧，」安娜答道，心想叫约翰的人多的是。

说不定汉斯的好朋友也是呢。「眼睛什么颜色？」克斯托夫追问。「梦幻。」安娜微笑着说。「你跟他一起吃过饭没有？」克斯托夫问，「万一你讨厌他吃饭的样子怎么办？」

「万一你讨厌他挖鼻孔的样子呢？」安娜皱起眉头。「挖鼻孔？」「还吃下去，」克斯托夫补了一句。「恕我直言，先生，」安娜说，「他可是位王子。」克斯托夫摇了摇头。「男人都那样。」「噫——！」安娜做了个鬼脸，「听着，这都不重要。」

「这是真爱。」「听起来可不像真爱，」克斯托夫直视前方说道。「你是什么恋爱专家吗？」安娜问。「不是，但我有朋友是，」他答道。「你还有当恋爱专家的朋友？」安娜嘲讽地问。

克斯托夫瞪大了眼睛，停下了雪橇。「别说了，」他命令道。「不，我倒想见见这些朋友，」她咧嘴笑着坚持道。

克斯托夫伸手捂住了安娜的嘴。「我是认真的。」

「嘘——！」他站起身，望向幽暗的树林。

他举起一盏灯笼。

忽然，他大喊起来：「斯文！」

「走！」

「快走！」雪橇猛地冲了出去，安娜向后摔倒。

她看见四周的黑暗中亮起一双双眼睛。「那是什么？」她低声问。「狼，」克斯托夫说。「我们怎么办？」安娜问。

她看着克斯托夫，做好了准备。「交给我，」克斯托夫镇定地说，「你只要不掉下去——也别被吃掉就行。」「可我想帮忙，」安娜说。「不行，」克斯托夫答道。「为什么不行？」安娜撅起嘴。「因为我不信任你的判断力，」克斯托夫说。

安娜被激怒了。「你说什么？」一只狼扑向雪橇，克斯托夫一脚把它踢了回去。「谁会嫁给一个刚认识的人啊？」安娜气得发抖，「这是真爱！」她抄起克斯托夫的鲁特琴，朝他的头挥了过去。

他一低头，安娜那一下正好打中了一只正要扑上雪橇的狼！「哇哦！」克斯托夫惊呼，可就在这时，另一只狼跳起来把他撞倒了。

他摔了出去，被雪橇拖在后面。「克里斯托弗！」安娜喊道。「是克斯托夫！」他大叫。

安娜拿起灯笼，把雪橇上的毛毯点着了火。

她把燃着的毛毯朝克斯托夫扔去，狼群纷纷从他身上翻落。

接着她伸手把他拉回了雪橇上。

克斯托夫懊恼地看着她。「你差点把我点着了，」他说。「可我没有，」安娜答道。

斯文忽然嘶鸣起来。

他前方是一道陡降的悬崖，下方便是巨大的峡谷。「准备起跳，斯文！」安娜喊道。「你少指挥他！」克斯托夫吼道。「我偏要！」他一个利落的动作，抓起安娜甩到了斯文背上。

接着他解开了驯鹿的挽具。「跳！」斯文纵身一跃，背着安娜越过了峡谷。

紧跟在他们身后，克斯托夫勇敢地带着雪橇一起跃起。

雪橇没能完全越过，但在它坠入峡谷前一刻，克斯托夫自己跳了出去，抓住了对岸的崖边。

在他悬在崖壁下方时，他那崭新的雪橇在下面燃起了火焰。「我刚买到的。」他叹了口气朝下望去。

接着，他的手开始在光滑的冰面上打滑。「呃——哦，」他惊慌地说，「不，不，不！」不知从哪儿飞来一把斧头，猛地扎进离他脸只有几寸远的雪里。

他听到安娜的声音从上方传来。「抓住！」她喊道。

斧头系着一根绳子，绳子绕在斯文身上。「拉，斯文！」安娜下令道。

斯文用力往后拉，倒退着走，把克斯托夫拽到了安全处。

安娜和克斯托夫俯身望着崖边燃烧的雪橇。「我会赔你这架雪橇，还有里面的所有东西，」她承诺道。

她难过地看着克斯托夫。「而且，如果你不想再帮我了，我也理解。」克斯托夫看着安娜走远。

斯文用冰凉的鼻子轻轻蹭了蹭他。「我当然不想再帮她了，」他对驯鹿说，「说真的，这整件事让我再也不想帮任何人了。」他看着安娜转身朝相反方向走去。「可她一个人会死掉的，」他压低嗓子，用斯文那低沉的嗓音说道。

克斯托夫别过脸去。「那我也认了，」他说。

安娜转来转去，不知该往哪走。「可她要是死了，你就拿不到新雪橇了，」克斯托夫继续用斯文的嗓音说。

他叹了口气。「等一下，」他用自己本来的声音朝安娜喊道，「我们来了。」安娜咧嘴一笑。「你们来？」她高兴地说。

接着她定了定神。「我是说，当然，我允许你跟着。」安娜不知道前路如何，却很高兴克斯托夫和斯文能陪她同去。

chapters.title: 第十二章 · 山巅远眺
chapters.en:
Together, Kristoff, Sven, and Anna walked through the night. As dawn crept over the horizon, the three travelers found themselves on the rim of a mountain. Looking down, they could see Arendelle in the distance.

But it wasn’t the summertime view they were expecting. The kingdom was completely frozen, covered with white ice.

Anna gasped in shock. Then she pulled herself together. “It’ll be fine,” she said. “Elsa will thaw it.”

“Will she?” Kristoff asked skeptically. “Just like that?”

“Sure,” Anna replied. She pointed straight ahead. “Come on. This way to the North Mountain, right?”

“More like this way,” Kristoff said, pushing her pointing finger upward. A huge, steep mountain towered above them.

With no other choice, the group continued, moving forward and up. As the sun finally rose completely, they rounded a corner and came upon a clearing surrounded by tall trees.

They gasped as the morning light danced on the snowy area before them. The terrain was different from what they had seen in the rest of the woods. They had found a gorgeous winter wonderland.

The view took Anna’s breath away. “I never knew winter could be so…beautiful,” she said, looking up at a willow tree covered in ice. The branches looked as if they were glistening with a crystal coating. Then she noticed Sven. The reindeer had gotten his antlers tangled up in icy vines, and he looked like a twinkling Christmas tree!

“Yeah, but it’s so white!” said a voice that came out of nowhere. “Does it hurt your eyes? My eyes are killing me. You know, how about a little color?”

Anna and Kristoff looked around. They stared at Sven for a moment. Could he be the one speaking?

“Must we bleach the joy out of it all?” the voice went on. “I’m thinking like maybe some crimson or chartreuse. How about yellow? No, not yellow. Yellow and snow? Brrrr… No-go.”

A goofy little snowman with twigs for arms, but no nose, appeared. He laughed at his own yellow snow joke. “Am I right?” he asked Anna.

“AAAAHHH!” Anna screamed. She’d never seen a talking snowman before, and she reacted quickly. She kicked him in the snowball head, which went flying right into Kristoff.

“Hi!” the snowman head said.

“You’re creepy,” Kristoff told the head. He tossed it to Anna.

“I don’t want it!” Anna shrieked, throwing it back to Kristoff.

“Back at you!” Kristoff called, chucking the head to her again.

“Please don’t drop me!” the snowman head pleaded.

Anna frowned at Kristoff. “Don’t!”

Kristoff grinned. “Come on, it’s just a head,” he said.

“All right,” the snowman told them. “We got off to a bad start.”

“The body!” Anna cried. She quickly dropped the head onto the body, but somehow it landed upside down—and stuck that way.

“Wait!” the snowman said, gazing at the upside-down world around him. “What am I looking at right now? Why are you hanging off the earth like a bat?”

Anna walked over to the snowman. “All right,” she said. “Wait one second.” She turned his head around so he was right-side up.

“Oh, thank you!” he said.

“You’re welcome,” Anna said, smiling at the little snowman. He wasn’t so scary now that she’d gotten a chance to look at him properly.

“Now I’m perfect,” the snowman said.

“Well, almost,” Anna replied. She grabbed a carrot from Sven’s pack and pushed it into Olaf’s face to give him a nose. She pushed a little too forcefully, though, and the carrot went right through his head! “Oh, too hard!” Anna said. “I’m sorry! I—I was just…”

The snowman spun around. “Woo!” he exclaimed. “Head rush!”

Anna bent down to him. “Are you okay?”

He beamed. Even though only a tiny point of the carrot was sticking out in front, he was happy. “Are you kidding me?” he asked. “I am wonderful! I’ve always wanted a nose.” He looked down, cross-eyed, at his new feature. “So cute. It’s like a little baby unicorn.”

With another shove, Anna pushed the carrot from the back of his head so the carrot nose was in the proper place.

“What? Hey! Whoa!” the snowman cried out. “I love it even more! All right, let’s start this thing over.” A smile spread across his face. “Hi, everyone! I’m Olaf, and I like warm hugs.” He opened his twig arms wide for a hug.

The name struck Anna. “Olaf?” she asked. Anna thought for a moment. She remembered building a little snowman with Elsa when they were young. Elsa had given that snowman the same name.

Olaf gazed at Anna. “And you are?”

“I’m Anna,” she answered.

“And who is the funky-looking donkey over there?” Olaf inquired.

“That’s Sven,” Anna told him.

“Uh-huh,” Olaf said. “And who’s the reindeer?”

“Sven!” Anna said, laughing at Olaf’s mistake.

Confused, Olaf stared at both Sven and Kristoff, thinking they had the same name. “Oh, okay. Makes things easier for me,” he said.

Sven moved closer to the talking snowman and tried to take a bite of Olaf’s carrot nose.

“Aww,” Olaf said, laughing. “Look at him, trying to kiss my nose.” He smiled at the reindeer. “I like you, too!”

“Olaf, did Elsa build you?” Anna asked.

“Yeah, why?” the snowman replied.

“Do you know where she is?” Anna said, moving closer.

“Yeah, why?” Olaf said, innocently oblivious to the line of questioning.

“Do you think you could show us the way?” Anna asked, full of hope.

“Yeah, why?” the snowman asked again.

Kristoff was busy examining one of Olaf’s twig arms, which had fallen off. “How does this work?”

The hand on the arm smacked Kristoff across the face!

“Stop it, Sven!” Olaf said, calling Kristoff by the wrong name. “We need to focus here!” He turned to face Anna. “Why?”

“I’ll tell you why,” Kristoff said. “We need Elsa to bring back summer.”

“Summer?” Olaf said. “Oh, I don’t know why, but I’ve always loved the idea of summer and sun, and all things hot!”

Kristoff raised his eyebrows. “Really? I’m guessing you don’t have much experience with heat.”

Olaf shook his head. “Nope, but sometimes I like to close my eyes and imagine what it’d be like when summer does come.”

As Olaf went on and on about all the wonderful things he would do in summer, Kristoff looked over at Anna. “I’m going to tell him,” he whispered. It was killing him to hear Olaf talk about summer’s heat—which is a snowman’s worst nightmare!

“Don’t you dare,” Anna scolded Kristoff. She couldn’t bear to ruin Olaf’s dream with the harsh truth.

Olaf took Anna’s hand. “So come on! Let’s go bring back summer!”

“I’m coming!” Anna said. She looked over her shoulder at Kristoff.

“Somebody’s got to tell him,” Kristoff murmured, shaking his head. He and Sven followed Anna and the little snowman.
chapters.zh:
克斯托夫、斯文和安娜一起在夜色中赶路。

当晨曦悄悄爬上地平线，三位旅人发觉自己已来到一处山脊上。

向下望去，他们能远远望见阿伦黛尔。

可那并不是他们期待中的夏日景象。

整个王国冻得严严实实，覆着一层白冰。

安娜震惊得倒抽一口气。

接着她定了定神。「会没事的，」她说，「艾莎会把冰融化的。」「她会吗？」克斯托夫将信将疑地问，「就这么简单？」「当然，」安娜答道。

她笔直指向前方。「走吧。」

「去北山是这条路，对吧？」「更像是这边，」克斯托夫说着，把她的手指往上推了推。

一座巨大而陡峭的山峰高耸在他们头顶。

别无选择，这支小队继续前行，一路向上。

当太阳终于完全升起，他们转过一个弯，来到一片被高大树木环绕的空地。

晨光在眼前这片雪地上起舞，他们看得屏住了呼吸。

这里的地形与他们之前在林中见到的截然不同。

他们发现了一处美不胜收的冬日仙境。

眼前的景致令安娜惊叹不已。「我从不知道冬天可以这么……美，」她仰头望着一棵覆满冰晶的柳树说道。

那些枝条仿佛镀上了一层水晶外壳，闪闪发亮。

接着她注意到了斯文。

驯鹿的角缠进了冰藤里，看上去就像一棵闪闪发光的圣诞树！「是挺美，可这也太白了！」一个不知从哪儿冒出来的声音说，「刺得你眼睛疼吗？」

「我的眼睛都要瞎了。」

「我说，来点颜色怎么样？」安娜和克斯托夫四下张望。

他们盯着斯文看了一会儿。

会是他在说话吗？「非得把这点乐趣都漂成惨白吗？」那声音继续道，「我在想，也许来点深红或者黄绿。」

「黄色怎么样？」

「不，不要黄色。」

「黄色配雪？」

「哆——不要。」一个傻乎乎的小雪人出现了，他用树枝当胳膊，却没有鼻子。

他对自己那句「黄雪」的笑话笑了起来。「我说得对吧？」他问安娜。「啊——啊！」安娜尖叫起来。

她从没见过会说话的雪人，反应十分迅速。

她一脚踢中他的雪球脑袋，脑袋飞出去正好砸中克斯托夫。「嗨！」雪人脑袋说。「你真瘆人，」克斯托夫对那颗脑袋说。

他把脑袋抛给安娜。「我才不要！」安娜尖叫着，把它抛回给克斯托夫。「还给你！」克斯托夫叫着，又把脑袋扔回给她。「求你们别把我扔了！」雪人脑袋哀求道。

安娜朝克斯托夫皱起眉。「别扔！」克斯托夫咧嘴一笑。「得了，不过就是颗脑袋嘛，」他说。「好吧，」雪人对他们说，「咱们的开头可不怎么样。」「身体！」安娜喊道。

她慌忙把脑袋安到身体上，可不知怎么，它倒着落了上去——而且还卡住了。「等等！」雪人望着四周上下颠倒的世界说，「我现在看到的是啥？」

「你干嘛像蝙蝠似的挂在地上？」安娜走到雪人跟前。「好了，」她说，「等一下。」她把他的脑袋转过来，让他正了过来。「噢，谢谢你！」他说。「不客气，」安娜微笑着对这个小雪人说。

既然有机会好好看清楚，他也没那么吓人了。「现在我完美了，」雪人说。「嗯，差不多吧，」安娜答道。

她从斯文的背包里取出一根胡萝卜，朝雪宝脸上按去，想给他安个鼻子。

可她用力稍重了些，胡萝卜直接穿过了他的脑袋！「噢，太用力了！」安娜说，「对不起！」

「我——我只是……」雪人转了个圈。「呜呼！」他惊叫，「一阵头晕！」安娜弯下腰问他。「你还好吗？」他咧嘴一笑。

尽管胡萝卜只有小小的一截露在前面，他依然高兴。「你开玩笑吧？」他问，「我好得很！」

「我一直想要个鼻子。」他斗鸡眼似地低头看着自己的新器官。「真可爱。」

「就像一只小独角兽。」安娜又推了一把，从他脑后把胡萝卜往前推，让胡萝卜鼻子归到了该在的位置。「什么？」

「嘿！」

「哇哦！」雪人大声叫道，「我更喜欢了！」

「好啦，咱们重新来过吧。」他脸上绽开笑容。「嗨，大家好！」

「我是雪宝，我喜欢温暖的拥抱。」他张开树枝做的双臂，准备拥抱。

这个名字让安娜心头一震。「雪宝？」她问。

安娜想了一会儿。

她想起小时候和艾莎一起堆过一个小雪人。

艾莎给那个雪人起了同样的名字。

雪宝打量着安娜。「那你呢？」「我是安娜，」她答道。「那边那头长相奇怪的驴是谁？」雪宝好奇地问。「那是斯文，」安娜告诉他。「嗯哼，」雪宝说，「那驯鹿又是谁？」「斯文！」安娜说，被雪宝的搞错逗笑了。

搞糊涂了的雪宝盯着斯文和克斯托夫看了半天，以为他俩同名。「噢，好吧。」

「这样对我来说省事了，」他说。

斯文凑近会说话的雪人，想咬一口雪宝的胡萝卜鼻子。「哎呀，」雪宝笑着说道，「瞧他，想亲我的鼻子呢。」他对驯鹿笑了笑。「我也喜欢你！」「雪宝，你是艾莎造出来的吗？」安娜问。「是啊，怎么了？」雪人答道。「你知道她在哪儿吗？」安娜边说边凑近了些。「知道啊，怎么了？」雪宝天真地对这番盘问毫无察觉。「你能带我们去吗？」安娜满怀希望地问。「行啊，怎么了？」雪人又问。

克斯托夫正忙着研究雪宝掉下来的一根树枝胳膊。「这是怎么运作的？」胳膊上的手「啪」地扇在了克斯托夫脸上！「别闹了，斯文！」雪宝叫错了克斯托夫的名字，「我们要专心！」他转过身面对安娜。「为什么？」「我来告诉你为什么，」克斯托夫说，「我们需要艾莎把夏天带回来。」「夏天？」雪宝说，「噢，我也不知为啥，可我一直喜欢夏天、太阳，还有一切热乎乎的东西！」克斯托夫扬起眉毛。「真的吗？」

「我猜你没怎么感受过热吧。」雪宝摇了摇头。「没有，不过有时候我喜欢闭上眼睛，想象夏天真的到来时会是什么样。」雪宝滔滔不绝地说着夏天里要做的一切美妙之事，克斯托夫则扭头看向安娜。「我要告诉他，」他低声说。

听雪宝谈论夏天的炎热，简直让克斯托夫受不了——那可是雪人最可怕的噩梦！「你敢，」安娜责备克斯托夫。

她不忍心用残酷的真相毁掉雪宝的梦想。

雪宝拉起安娜的手。「那就走吧！」

「咱们去把夏天找回来！」「我来啦！」安娜说。

她回头瞥了克斯托夫一眼。「总得有人告诉他，」克斯托夫摇着头喃喃道。

他和斯文跟着安娜和小雪人走去。
